deck_name: 君の名は。 Ch.2 端緒 — Core Words
source: 新海誠『君の名は。』(角川つばさ文庫), 第二章「端緒」
notes: Everyday words (mostly N4–N3, plus common N2 words and set phrases) for Chapter 2. Study this deck first. Chapter 2 starts on p.9. Cards from pp.9 and 12–21 are checked against the printed pages and come first, in page order (pp.10–11 weren't photographed; their cards are marked). Cards after that are built from the chapter's scenes and the novel's style and say 'Not yet checked' in their scene — some of them may turn out to belong to Chapter 3. Example sentences are original, not quoted from the book.

priority_guide.high: Learn before or while reading this chapter — it carries the scene.
priority_guide.medium: Useful; context usually helps if you forget it.
priority_guide.low: Recognition is enough — look it up once, don't over-drill.

difficulty_guide.two_above: N1 / literary — ambitious; learn to recognise it.

kanji_difficulty_guide.easy: Kanji are common; readable at N3.
kanji_difficulty_guide.medium: One or more kanji may trip you — drill the reading.
kanji_difficulty_guide.hard: Rare kanji or irregular reading — learn the kana form first.

cards.scene: p.9 — 瀧 got so absorbed in drawing that he went to bed at dawn.
cards.context: Literally 'inside a dream'. 〜に夢中になる = to be absorbed in / crazy about (ゲームに夢中). 夢中で〜 = frantically, without stopping to think (夢中で走る).
cards.example_sentence: 弟はゲームに夢中で、呼んでも返事をしない。
cards.example_reading: おとうと は ゲーム に むちゅう で、 よんで も へんじ を しない。
cards.example_meaning: My little brother is so absorbed in his game that he doesn't answer when I call.

cards.scene: p.9 — the girl's voice sounds close to tears (泣き出しそう).
cards.context: 泣く + 出す (suddenly start) — same pattern as 走り出す, 笑い出す. 泣き顔 = a crying face; 泣き虫 = a crybaby.
cards.example_sentence: 犬がほえると、赤ちゃんが泣き出した。
cards.example_reading: いぬ が ほえる と、 あかちゃん が なきだした。
cards.example_meaning: When the dog barked, the baby burst into tears.

cards.scene: p.9 — suddenly the train stops; p.14 the haze lifts suddenly.
cards.context: Adverb or な-adjective: 突然の雨 = a sudden shower. 急に is more casual and also covers quick changes in state (急に寒くなった). 突 (thrust) + 然 (state).
cards.example_sentence: 晴れていたのに、突然雨が降り出した。
cards.example_reading: はれて いた のに、 とつぜん あめ が ふりだした。
cards.example_meaning: It had been sunny, but suddenly it started to rain.

cards.scene: p.9 — the moment he realises he's on a train.
cards.context: 〜に気づく = to notice (particle に). Also written 気付く; same meaning as 気がつく. 気づかないふりをする = to pretend not to notice. 気がつく means the same and is a little more colloquial.
cards.example_sentence: すぐ後ろに友達がいたのに、全然気づかなかった。
cards.example_reading: すぐ うしろ に ともだち が いた のに、 ぜんぜん きづかなかった。
cards.example_meaning: My friend was right behind me, but I didn't notice at all.

cards.scene: p.9 — the moment he realises where he is.
cards.context: Vた瞬間(に) = the moment that…: ドアを開けた瞬間. その瞬間 = at that very moment. 一瞬 (いっしゅん) measures a flash of time ('for an instant'); 瞬間 points at the moment itself.
cards.example_sentence: ドアを開けた瞬間、猫が外に飛び出した。
cards.example_reading: ドア を あけた しゅんかん、 ねこ が そと に とびだした。
cards.example_meaning: The moment I opened the door, the cat dashed outside.

cards.scene: p.9 — still half-asleep, 瀧 hears a bell he doesn't recognise and wonders if it's his alarm.
cards.context: Short for 目覚まし時計 (alarm clock), from 目を覚ます (to wake up). 目覚ましをかける = to set an alarm; 目覚ましが鳴る = the alarm goes off; 目覚ましを止める = to switch it off.
cards.example_sentence: 目覚ましを七時にかけたのに、鳴らなかった。
cards.example_reading: めざまし を しちじ に かけた のに、 なら なかった。
cards.example_meaning: I set the alarm for seven, but it didn't go off.

cards.scene: p.9 — 瀧 is still sleepy because he got absorbed in drawing last night.
cards.context: Same kanji, two readings: ゆうべ is the everyday spoken word, さくや is more formal and written (news, narration) — the book's furigana gives さくや. Also 昨晩 (さくばん). Compare 昨日 (きのう, formal さくじつ).
cards.example_sentence: 昨夜から降り続いた雪で、町は真っ白になった。
cards.example_reading: さくや から ふりつづいた ゆき で、 まち は まっしろ に なった。
cards.example_meaning: The town turned completely white with the snow that had been falling since last night.

cards.scene: p.9 — 瀧 only went to bed at dawn after drawing all night, which is why he can't wake up.
cards.context: From 明ける (night or a year comes to an end): 夜が明ける = day breaks; 明けましておめでとう uses the same verb. 〜方 (がた) = around that time, as in its opposite 夕方. 夜明け is the moment of daybreak; 明け方 is the stretch of time around it.
cards.example_sentence: 明け方まで勉強して、授業中に寝てしまった。
cards.example_reading: あけがた まで べんきょう して、 じゅぎょうちゅう に ねて しまった。
cards.example_meaning: I studied until dawn and ended up falling asleep in class.

cards.scene: pp.10–11 (not photographed yet) — With no warning at all, 瀧 wakes up in a stranger's body, and 三葉 wakes up in his.
cards.context: いきなり = abruptly, skipping the usual steps: いきなり怒り出す = to suddenly start shouting. 急に = suddenly (a change); 突然 (とつぜん) is a little more formal. The kanji 行き成り is rare.
cards.example_sentence: 歩いていたら、いきなり雨が降り出した。
cards.example_reading: あるいて いたら、 いきなり あめ が ふりだした。
cards.example_meaning: I was walking along when it suddenly started to rain.

cards.scene: pp.10–11 (not photographed yet) — 瀧 wakes up on a futon on the floor of 三葉's room, not in his own bed.
cards.context: 布団を敷く (しく) = to lay out the futon; 布団をたたむ = to fold it away. 掛け布団 = the top quilt, 敷き布団 = the mattress. ベッド is the Western-style bed 瀧 is used to.
cards.example_sentence: 朝起きたら、布団をたたんで押し入れにしまう。
cards.example_reading: あさ おきたら、 ふとん を たたんで おしいれ に しまう。
cards.example_meaning: When I get up in the morning, I fold up the futon and put it away in the closet.

cards.scene: pp.10–11 (not photographed yet) — 瀧 opens his eyes and nothing around him looks familiar: not the room, not the window, not the body.
cards.context: 見る + 慣れる (to get used to) → 見慣れる = to be used to seeing; 見慣れない = something you aren't used to seeing. 見慣れた景色 = a familiar view. Plainer than the hard deck's 見知らぬ.
cards.example_sentence: 駅を出ると、見慣れない景色が広がっていた。
cards.example_reading: えき を でる と、 みなれない けしき が ひろがって いた。
cards.example_meaning: When I came out of the station, an unfamiliar scene spread out before me.

cards.scene: pp.10–11 (not photographed yet) — What on earth is going on? 瀧 keeps asking himself this all through the strange morning.
cards.context: Goes with a question word and adds surprise or frustration: 一体何?, 一体どうして? = what / why on earth? As a noun, 一体 also means 'one body, a whole' (一体になる = to become one).
cards.example_sentence: こんな夜中に、一体誰が電話してきたんだろう。
cards.example_reading: こんな よなか に、 いったい だれ が でんわ して きた ん だろう。
cards.example_meaning: Who on earth could be calling in the middle of the night?

cards.scene: pp.10–11 (not photographed yet) — 瀧 decides this must be a dream. It can't be reality.
cards.context: 夢 (dream) vs 現実 (reality). 現実的 = realistic; 非現実的 = unrealistic; 現実に戻る = to come back to reality.
cards.example_sentence: 夢のような話だが、これは現実だ。
cards.example_reading: ゆめ の ような はなし だ が、 これ は げんじつ だ。
cards.example_meaning: It sounds like a dream, but this is reality.

cards.scene: pp.10–11 (not photographed yet) — Is this body real? 瀧 can hardly believe that what he sees and feels is genuine.
cards.context: 本 (true) + 物 (thing). Opposite: 偽物 (にせもの) = a fake. 本物の〜 = a real ~: 本物の革 = real leather.
cards.example_sentence: このかばんは安かったけど、本物の革だそうだ。
cards.example_reading: この かばん は やすかった けど、 ほんもの の かわ だ そう だ。
cards.example_meaning: This bag was cheap, but apparently it's real leather.

cards.scene: pp.10–11 (not photographed yet) — 瀧 checks the face in the mirror and the body he's in, to make sure of what he's seeing.
cards.context: 確かめる = to check something with your own eyes or hands. Related: 確か = certain / if I remember right; 確かに = certainly. 確認する (かくにん) is the more formal word.
cards.example_sentence: 家を出る前に、鍵をかけたかもう一度確かめた。
cards.example_reading: いえ を でる まえ に、 かぎ を かけた か もう いちど たしかめた。
cards.example_meaning: Before leaving the house, I checked once more that I'd locked the door.

cards.scene: pp.10–11 (not photographed yet) — Both of them panic in someone else's body, and keep rushing to cover their mistakes.
cards.context: 慌てる = to lose your calm and rush. 慌てて = hurriedly, in a panic (慌てて家を出た). 慌てないで = don't panic. 急ぐ just means 'to hurry', with no panic in it.
cards.example_sentence: 電車の時間を間違えて、慌てて駅まで走った。
cards.example_reading: でんしゃ の じかん を まちがえて、 あわてて えき まで はしった。
cards.example_meaning: I got the train time wrong and ran to the station in a panic.

cards.scene: p.12 — 瀧 has his hand on 三葉's chest when 四葉 walks in.
cards.context: Both the body part and where feelings sit: 胸が痛む = your heart aches; 胸がどきどきする = your heart pounds. 胸を張る = to puff out your chest with pride.
cards.example_sentence: 発表の前は、緊張で胸がどきどきした。
cards.example_reading: はっぴょう の まえ は、 きんちょう で むね が どきどき した。
cards.example_meaning: Before my presentation, my heart was pounding with nerves.

cards.scene: p.12 — 瀧 is (embarrassingly) moved by the body he's in.
cards.context: 感動する = to be moved (by a film, a view, someone's kindness). 感動的 = moving. Compare 感心 (admiring someone's skill) and 感激 (かんげき, overjoyed, a stronger word).
cards.example_sentence: その映画を見て、とても感動した。
cards.example_reading: その えいが を みて、 とても かんどう した。
cards.example_meaning: I was really moved by that film.

cards.scene: p.12 — 四葉 answers with an utterly fed-up expression.
cards.context: 表情が変わる = someone's expression changes; 表情が明るい = to look cheerful; 無表情 = expressionless. 顔色 (かおいろ) is complexion: 顔色が悪い = to look pale.
cards.example_sentence: 手紙を読んだ母の表情が、急に明るくなった。
cards.example_reading: てがみ を よんだ はは の ひょうじょう が、 きゅう に あかるく なった。
cards.example_meaning: My mother's face suddenly brightened when she read the letter.

cards.scene: pp.12–13 — he walks a few steps across the tatami to the mirror.
cards.context: Rooms are measured in mats: 六畳 (ろくじょう) = a six-mat room, with the counter read じょう. 和室 (わしつ) = a Japanese-style room. The verb 畳む (たたむ, to fold) uses the same kanji.
cards.example_sentence: 祖父の家には、畳の部屋が三つある。
cards.example_reading: そふ の いえ に は、 たたみ の へや が みっつ ある。
cards.example_meaning: My grandfather's house has three tatami rooms.

cards.scene: p.12 — caught with a hand on his chest, 瀧 just blurts out his honest impression when the girl asks what he's doing.
cards.context: な-adjective. 素直な感想 = an honest impression; 素直に言う / 素直に謝る = to say / apologise without making excuses. About a person it also means good-natured and obedient (素直な子). 正直 is about not lying; 素直 is about not resisting or putting up a front.
cards.example_sentence: 自分が悪かったと思ったら、素直に謝ったほうがいい。
cards.example_reading: じぶん が わるかった と おもったら、 すなおに あやまった ほう が いい。
cards.example_meaning: If you think you were in the wrong, you should just apologise.

cards.scene: p.12 — 瀧 says his frank impression of the body he's in, right in front of the little girl.
cards.context: What you think or feel after experiencing something: 映画の感想, 感想を言う, 感想文 (a book report). Don't mix it up with 感動 (being moved, on the same page) or 乾燥 (also かんそう, dryness).
cards.example_sentence: 映画を見たあと、友だちと感想を話し合った。
cards.example_reading: えいが を みた あと、 ともだち と かんそう を はなしあった。
cards.example_meaning: After the film, my friends and I talked about what we thought of it.

cards.scene: p.12 — 瀧 takes another look at the girl standing in the doorway.
cards.context: The written, narrative word for a girl (roughly school age to teens); in speech people say 女の子. The pair is 少年 (boy); 少女漫画 = girls' comics. Note it's 少 (few, young), not 小 (small).
cards.example_sentence: 窓の外で、一人の少女が猫と遊んでいた。
cards.example_reading: まど の そと で、 ひとり の しょうじょ が ねこ と あそんで いた。
cards.example_meaning: Outside the window, a girl was playing with a cat.

cards.scene: p.12 — after his first reply, 瀧 looks at the girl again, properly this time.
cards.context: Kanji 改めて, from 改める (to renew, change). Not just 'again': doing something again with fresh attention, or properly this time. あらためて見る, あらためて思う (to realise anew), あらためて連絡します (I'll get back to you later, in business).
cards.example_sentence: 卒業式の日、あらためて友だちの大切さを感じた。
cards.example_reading: そつぎょうしき の ひ、 あらためて ともだち の たいせつさ を かんじた。
cards.example_meaning: On graduation day, I felt anew how precious my friends were.

cards.scene: p.12 — 瀧 sizes up the girl: maybe ten, twin tails, upturned eyes, a cheeky-looking kid (生意気そう).
cards.context: な-adjective for someone, usually younger, acting above their place: 生意気な口をきく = to talk back. 生意気そう = looks cheeky (〜そう of appearance). Typically said by older siblings, teachers and seniors. Reading: 生 (なま) + 意気 (いき).
cards.example_sentence: 弟は最近、生意気なことばかり言う。
cards.example_reading: おとうと は さいきん、 なまいきな こと ばかり いう。
cards.example_meaning: My little brother says nothing but cheeky things lately.

cards.scene: p.12 — 瀧 points at himself and asks the girl if she means him when she says 'big sister'.
cards.context: 指 (finger) + さす (point): pointing with your finger. Also written 指差す. Plain 指す can point with anything (a clock hand) or mean 'refer to'. The book uses the stem as a link: 指さし、問う = points and asks.
cards.example_sentence: 子どもが空を指さして「飛行機！」と叫んだ。
cards.example_reading: こども が そら を ゆびさして 「ひこうき！」 と さけんだ。
cards.example_meaning: The child pointed at the sky and shouted, "A plane!"

cards.scene: p.12 — something at the corner of 瀧's vision catches his attention.
cards.context: An inside corner: 部屋の隅 (corner of the room), 視界の隅 (edge of your field of vision). A corner you turn, like a street corner, is 角 (かど). 隅々まで = every nook and cranny; 隅に置けない = surprisingly capable (lit. can't be left in the corner).
cards.example_sentence: 部屋の隅に、古いギターが置いてあった。
cards.example_reading: へや の すみ に、 ふるい ギター が おいて あった。
cards.example_meaning: An old guitar had been left in the corner of the room.

cards.scene: p.13 — standing at the mirror, 瀧 slides the loose pajamas off his shoulders.
cards.context: Opposite of きつい (tight). Clothes: 緩いズボン; also rules (緩いルール = lax), slopes (緩い坂 = gentle) and knots. Verbs: 緩む (come loose), 緩める (loosen: ネクタイを緩める). Often written in kana; ゆるキャラ (laid-back mascots) comes from it.
cards.example_sentence: 痩せたので、ズボンがだいぶ緩くなった。
cards.example_reading: やせた ので、 ズボン が だいぶ ゆるく なった。
cards.example_meaning: I've lost weight, so my trousers have got quite loose.

cards.scene: p.13 — 瀧 slides the pajamas off his shoulders and lets them fall.
cards.context: Transitive (you shift something); the intransitive partner is ずれる (to slip out of place). Physical: 机を少しずらす, 肩からずらす. Time: 予定を一日ずらす (push back a day), 時間をずらす (stagger the times).
cards.example_sentence: 会議を一時間ずらしてもらえますか。
cards.example_reading: かいぎ を いちじかん ずらして もらえます か。
cards.example_meaning: Could we push the meeting back an hour?

cards.scene: p.13 — the pajamas drop and 瀧 is left standing naked in front of the mirror.
cards.context: 裸になる = to get undressed. Related: 裸足 (はだし, barefoot), 裸眼 (らがん, without glasses), 丸裸 (stark naked; stripped of everything). The kanji has the clothing radical 衣 on the left.
cards.example_sentence: 夏になると、弟は裸で家の中を走り回る。
cards.example_reading: なつ に なる と、 おとうと は はだか で いえ の なか を はしりまわる。
cards.example_meaning: In summer, my little brother runs around the house naked.

meanings: to appear (in a mirror / on a screen)
cards.scene: p.13 — 瀧 stares at the whole body reflected in the mirror.
cards.context: 映る = to appear as an image: in a mirror, on water, on TV (鏡に映る, テレビに映る). Different from 写る (to come out in a photo: 写真に写る) and 移る (to move). Transitive: 映す (to reflect, to show on a screen).
cards.example_sentence: 湖の水面に、山がきれいに映っている。
cards.example_reading: みずうみ の すいめん に、 やま が きれいに うつって いる。
cards.example_meaning: The mountains are beautifully reflected on the surface of the lake.

cards.scene: p.13 — 瀧 takes in the whole body in the mirror, from head to toe.
cards.context: 全 (whole) + 身 (body). 全身が痛い (to ache all over), 全身鏡 (full-length mirror), 全身全霊 (with body and soul). Same sound as 前進 (ぜんしん, moving forward).
cards.example_sentence: 久しぶりに運動したら、次の日、全身が筋肉痛になった。
cards.example_reading: ひさしぶり に うんどう したら、 つぎ の ひ、 ぜんしん が きんにくつう に なった。
cards.example_meaning: I exercised for the first time in ages, and the next day my whole body ached.

cards.scene: p.13 — the long black hair in the mirror is sticking up here and there with bedhead.
cards.context: Kanji 所々 (々 repeats the kanji). Scattered spots, not everywhere: ところどころ破れている, ところどころ雪が残る. あちこち is similar but stresses many places; ところどころ stresses 'only in spots'.
cards.example_sentence: 古い地図は、ところどころ字が消えて読めなかった。
cards.example_reading: ふるい ちず は、 ところどころ じ が きえて よめなかった。
cards.example_meaning: The old map had faded in places, and I couldn't read the writing.

cards.scene: p.13 — the lips in the mirror have a cheerful sort of shape.
cards.context: 唇をかむ = to bite your lip (frustration); 唇が荒れる = to get chapped lips. 口 is the whole mouth; 唇 is just the lips. Don't confuse with 舌 (した, tongue).
cards.example_sentence: 冬は空気が乾燥して、唇が荒れやすい。
cards.example_reading: ふゆ は くうき が かんそう して、 くちびる が あれやすい。
cards.example_meaning: In winter the air is dry, so your lips chap easily.

cards.scene: p.13 — 瀧 jokes that the chest seems to announce 'thanks to you, I grew up healthy!'
cards.context: お陰様で: a polite reply when asked about your health or a success, thanking people in general even if they didn't literally help: 「お元気ですか」「おかげさまで」. Plain おかげで = thanks to / because of, and can be sarcastic (君のおかげで遅れた).
cards.example_sentence: 「お母さん、その後お元気ですか。」「おかげさまで、すっかりよくなりました。」
cards.example_reading: 「おかあさん、 その ご おげんき です か。」「おかげさまで、 すっかり よく なりました。」
cards.example_meaning: "How has your mother been since then?" "She's completely better, thank you."

cards.scene: p.13 — part of 瀧's joke: a body that has 'grown up healthy'.
cards.context: Noun and な-adjective: 健康な体, 健康に育つ (to grow up healthy), 健康診断 (health check-up), 健康のために (for your health). 元気 is more 'energetic, in good spirits'; 健康 is physical health specifically.
cards.example_sentence: 毎朝歩くようにしてから、前より健康になった。
cards.example_reading: まいあさ あるく ように して から、 まえ より けんこう に なった。
cards.example_meaning: Since I started walking every morning, I've become healthier than before.

cards.scene: p.13 — the faint shadows of the ribs; the word comes back on p.17 for the shadows on the mountains.
cards.context: 影 = a shadow cast by something, or a shape or silhouette. 陰 (also かげ) = shade, the side out of the sun (木陰, 日陰). Idioms: 影も形もない (not a trace), 影が薄い (easy to overlook; lit. a faint shadow).
cards.example_sentence: 夕方になると、自分の影が長く伸びる。
cards.example_reading: ゆうがた に なる と、 じぶん の かげ が ながく のびる。
cards.example_meaning: In the evening, your shadow stretches out long.

cards.scene: p.13 — below the ribs, the soft curve of the waist.
cards.context: 柔らか(な) is the な-adjective form of 柔らかい: same meaning, a touch more literary and common in description (柔らかな光, 柔らかな曲線). Also written 軟らかい for things that aren't hard (軟らかい肉). Opposite: 硬い / かたい.
cards.example_sentence: 春の柔らかな日差しが、窓から部屋いっぱいに差し込んだ。
cards.example_reading: はる の やわらかな ひざし が、 まど から へや いっぱい に さしこんだ。
cards.example_meaning: Soft spring sunlight poured through the window and filled the room.

cards.scene: p.13 — the soft curve of the waist in the mirror.
cards.context: 腰 covers the waist, hips and lower back: 腰が痛い (lower-back pain), 腰に手を当てる (hands on hips), 腰を下ろす (to sit down). Idioms: 腰が低い (humble), 本腰を入れる (to get serious about something).
cards.example_sentence: 重い荷物を持ったら、腰が痛くなった。
cards.example_reading: おもい にもつ を もったら、 こし が いたく なった。
cards.example_meaning: I carried something heavy and my lower back started to hurt.

cards.scene: p.13 — he's never seen one in person, but 瀧 knows this is without a doubt a girl's body.
cards.context: 間違い (mistake) + なく (without), so 'with no mistake'. It's a judgement based on facts, stronger than きっと (a confident guess). Same Nなく adverb pattern as in Ch.1. 間違いない = there's no doubt.
cards.example_sentence: このまま行けば、彼は間違いなく優勝するだろう。
cards.example_reading: この まま いけば、 かれ は まちがいなく ゆうしょう する だろう。
cards.example_meaning: If things go on like this, he'll definitely win.

cards.scene: p.14 — his head clears, panic sets in, and 瀧 screams.
cards.context: 叫ぶ = to cry out, usually with emotion; 大声を出す is just 'speak loudly'. 叫び声 = a scream.
cards.example_sentence: 山の上で、大きな声で名前を叫んだ。
cards.example_reading: やま の うえ で、 おおきな こえ で なまえ を さけんだ。
cards.example_meaning: At the top of the mountain, I shouted the name at the top of my voice.

cards.scene: p.14 — 瀧's head clears all at once, and then just as suddenly he panics.
cards.context: 一気に飲む = to drink in one gulp; 一気に読む = to read in one sitting. The book uses it twice in a row for effect: clear-headed all at once, then confused (混乱) all at once.
cards.example_sentence: おもしろくて、その本を一晩で一気に読んでしまった。
cards.example_reading: おもしろくて、 その ほん を ひとばん で いっきに よんで しまった。
cards.example_meaning: It was so good that I read the whole book in one night.

cards.scene: p.14 — 三葉 walks into the living room, where the family has breakfast.
cards.context: Same sound as 今 (now) — context tells them apart. 居 (いる, to be, stay) + 間 (room). A traditional word; modern flats tend to say リビング.
cards.example_sentence: 夕ご飯のあと、家族みんなで居間でテレビを見た。
cards.example_reading: ゆうごはん の あと、 かぞく みんな で いま で テレビ を みた。
cards.example_meaning: After dinner the whole family watched TV in the living room.

cards.scene: p.14 — 四葉 seems convinced she's the more responsible of the two sisters.
cards.context: Of a person, しっかりしている = dependable, mature, has their act together (often said of kids who act older than they are). As an adverb: しっかり持つ (hold tight), しっかり食べる (eat properly). しっかりして! = pull yourself together!
cards.example_sentence: 隣の家の子は小学生なのに、とてもしっかりしている。
cards.example_reading: となり の いえ の こ は しょうがくせい なのに、 とても しっかり して いる。
cards.example_meaning: The kid next door is only in primary school, but very responsible.

cards.scene: p.14 — 三葉 thinks apologising would mean showing weakness to her sister.
cards.context: 弱みを見せる = to show weakness; 弱みを握る = to have something on someone. Opposite: 強み (strength, strong point). 弱点 (じゃくてん) is the more technical 'weak spot'.
cards.example_sentence: ライバルの前では、絶対に弱みを見せたくない。
cards.example_reading: ライバル の まえ で は、 ぜったい に よわみ を みせたく ない。
cards.example_meaning: I never want to show weakness in front of my rival.

cards.scene: p.14 — The freshly cooked white rice glistens as 三葉 opens the cooker.
cards.context: ぴかぴかの靴 = shiny shoes; ぴかぴかの一年生 = a brand-new first-grader; ぴかぴかにみがく = polish till it shines. The book has ぴかぴかした白飯 (はくはん, plain white rice). Compare きらきら (twinkling) and ぴかっと (a single flash).
cards.example_sentence: 車を洗ったら、新車みたいにぴかぴかになった。
cards.example_reading: くるま を あらったら、 しんしゃ みたい に ぴかぴか に なった。
cards.example_meaning: After I washed the car, it was as shiny as a new one.

cards.scene: p.14 — 三葉 serves rice into her own bowl.
cards.context: Despite the 茶 (tea), a 茶碗 at home is the rice bowl (ご飯茶碗); everyday tea is drunk from a 湯のみ. Counter: 杯 — 茶碗一杯のご飯 (a bowl of rice). 碗 is a rare kanji, so learn the word as a unit.
cards.example_sentence: おなかがすいていたので、ご飯を茶碗二杯も食べた。
cards.example_reading: おなか が すいて いた ので、 ごはん を ちゃわん にはい も たべた。
cards.example_meaning: I was so hungry that I ate two whole bowls of rice.

cards.scene: p.15 — 四葉 grins knowingly at 三葉 about yesterday (サヤちん grins the same way on p.19).
cards.context: にやにや is a sly, teasing or knowing grin — usually a bit annoying for the person on the receiving end. にこにこ is a warm, happy smile. Verb: にやつく; the book also uses the noun にやつき.
cards.example_sentence: 弟が何かたくらんでいるような顔で、にやにやしている。
cards.example_reading: おとうと が なにか たくらんで いる よう な かお で、 にやにや して いる。
cards.example_meaning: My brother is smirking as if he's plotting something.

cards.scene: p.15 — 四葉 reminds 三葉 that yesterday she suddenly screamed for no reason.
cards.context: 悲鳴をあげる = to let out a scream (of fear, pain, surprise). 悲 (sad) + 鳴 (cry out). Figurative: うれしい悲鳴 = 'a nice problem to have'. The reader knows exactly whose scream it was — 瀧's, on p.14.
cards.example_sentence: 部屋に大きな虫が出て、姉は悲鳴をあげた。
cards.example_reading: へや に おおきな むし が でて、 あね は ひめい を あげた。
cards.example_meaning: A huge bug appeared in the room and my sister screamed.

cards.scene: p.15 — 三葉 is sure her little sister's smirk means she's making fun of her.
cards.context: 馬鹿にする, written in kana in this book. Stronger than からかう — it implies contempt. Passive: ばかにされる (to be made fun of). The book adds (に違いない) — 'must be mocking me'.
cards.example_sentence: 初めて料理をしたとき、兄にばかにされて悔しかった。
cards.example_reading: はじめて りょうり を した とき、 あに に ばか に されて くやしかった。
cards.example_meaning: When I cooked for the first time, my brother made fun of me and I was so annoyed.

cards.scene: p.15 — Grandma and 四葉 both stare at her, and 三葉 thinks: what is it with you two, so rude.
cards.context: Full form 感じが悪い = gives a bad impression; casual speech drops the が. Opposite: 感じがいい (pleasant, nice). The book has 二人そろって感じ悪い — そろって = both together.
cards.example_sentence: あの店員、こっちを見もしないで、なんか感じ悪いね。
cards.example_reading: あの てんいん、 こっち を み も しないで、 なんか かんじ わるい ね。
cards.example_meaning: That shop assistant didn't even look at us — kind of rude, right?

cards.scene: p.15 — The speaker comes on at a 'violent' volume.
cards.context: 音量を上げる / 下げる = to turn the volume up / down. 音 (sound) + 量 (amount). The book's 暴力的な音量 ('violent volume') is comic exaggeration.
cards.example_sentence: 夜なので、テレビの音量を少し下げてください。
cards.example_reading: よる なので、 テレビ の おんりょう を すこし さげて ください。
cards.example_meaning: It's late, so please turn the TV down a little.

cards.scene: p.15 — With a ピンポンパンポーン chime, the speaker sounds.
cards.context: Intransitive: ベルが鳴る, 電話が鳴る. Transitive: 鳴らす (to ring something). Same kanji as 鳴く (animals and birds cry) — 鳴る is for things, 鳴く for creatures.
cards.example_sentence: 授業中に、だれかの携帯電話が鳴った。
cards.example_reading: じゅぎょうちゅう に、 だれか の けいたい でんわ が なった。
cards.example_meaning: Someone's mobile phone rang during class.

cards.scene: p.15 — The announcer is the older sister of サヤちん, 三葉's best friend (we meet her on p.18).
cards.context: 親 here means 'intimate', as in 親しい (したしい, close). 親友 is stronger than 友達 — a friend you trust completely. 三葉, テッシー and サヤちん have been best friends for ten years.
cards.example_sentence: 困ったときは、いつも親友に相談する。
cards.example_reading: こまった とき は、 いつも しんゆう に そうだん する。
cards.example_meaning: Whenever I'm in trouble, I talk it over with my best friend.

cards.scene: p.16 — a shabby little town of 1,500 people.
cards.context: 人口が多い / 少ない (not 大きい). 人口が減る = the population falls.
cards.example_sentence: この村の人口は、千人もいない。
cards.example_reading: この むら の じんこう は、 せんにん も いない。
cards.example_meaning: This village has fewer than a thousand people.

cards.scene: p.16 — everyone is an acquaintance, or an acquaintance's acquaintance.
cards.context: 知り合い = someone you know, not necessarily a friend. 知り合う = to get to know each other; 知り合いの店 = a shop run by someone I know.
cards.example_sentence: パーティーには知り合いが一人もいなかった。
cards.example_reading: パーティー に は しりあい が ひとり も いなかった。
cards.example_meaning: I didn't know a single person at the party.

cards.scene: p.16 — speakers set up outdoors all over town.
cards.context: The book writes 町中 with the reading まちじゅう (all over town); read ちょうちゅう it means 'in town'. 〜じゅう (中) = throughout: 町じゅう, 世界じゅう, 一日じゅう (all day long). Often written 町中 — but 町中 read まちなか means 'in town, downtown', so watch the reading.
cards.example_sentence: その噂は、あっという間に町じゅうに広まった。
cards.example_reading: その うわさ は、 あっという ま に まちじゅう に ひろまった。
cards.example_meaning: The rumor spread all over town in no time.

cards.scene: p.16 — the town broadcast echoes off the mountains like a round.
cards.context: 放送する = to broadcast; 校内放送 = a school PA announcement; 放送部 = a school broadcasting club; 放送を流す = to put out an announcement. The main deck's 防災無線 is the town's emergency speaker system.
cards.example_sentence: 昼休みに、校内放送で私の名前が呼ばれた。
cards.example_reading: ひるやすみ に、 こうない ほうそう で わたし の なまえ が よばれた。
cards.example_meaning: At lunch break, my name was called over the school PA.

cards.scene: p.16 — the broadcast carries notices like the snow-shovelling rota.
cards.context: 連絡する = to contact, get in touch; 連絡を取る = to get in touch; 連絡先 = contact details. The set phrase 連絡がつかない (can't reach someone) has its own card in the grammar deck.
cards.example_sentence: 駅に着いたら、すぐ連絡してください。
cards.example_reading: えき に ついたら、 すぐ れんらく して ください。
cards.example_meaning: Please get in touch as soon as you reach the station.

cards.scene: p.16 — it even announces who was born and whose funeral is today (お葬式).
cards.context: 葬 (bury) + 式 (ceremony); polite お葬式. Related: 葬儀 (そうぎ, formal word), 通夜 (つや, the wake the night before), 喪服 (もふく, mourning clothes), 喪主 (もしゅ, chief mourner).
cards.example_sentence: 雨の中、たくさんの人が葬式に集まった。
cards.example_reading: あめ の なか、 たくさん の ひと が そうしき に あつまった。
cards.example_meaning: Despite the rain, many people gathered for the funeral.

cards.scene: p.16 — grandmother pulls the plug, silently showing her anger.
cards.context: Same kanji as 怒る (おこる), but the noun reads いかり. 怒りを感じる = to feel anger; 怒りを抑える (おさえる) = to hold in one's anger. The main deck's 込み上げる often goes with it.
cards.example_sentence: 不公平な決定に、多くの人が怒りの声を上げた。
cards.example_reading: ふこうへいな けってい に、 おおく の ひと が いかり の こえ を あげた。
cards.example_meaning: Many people voiced their anger at the unfair decision.

cards.scene: p.16 — In a town this small, most people know each other.
cards.context: Before a noun with の: 大抵の人 = most people. As an adverb: 大抵 = usually (日曜は大抵家にいる). Often written in kana; 抵 looks unfamiliar, so drill the reading.
cards.example_sentence: 大抵の店は、夜八時には閉まってしまう。
cards.example_reading: たいてい の みせ は、 よる はちじ に は しまって しまう。
cards.example_meaning: Most shops close by eight in the evening.

cards.scene: p.16 — Everyone in town is an acquaintance, or else a friend of a friend.
cards.context: A written-register 'or' (或いは), close to または / それとも. Also 'perhaps' in あるいは〜かもしれない. The book: あるいは知り合いの知り合い — or an acquaintance's acquaintance.
cards.example_sentence: 申し込みは、電話あるいはメールでお願いします。
cards.example_reading: もうしこみ は、 でんわ あるいは メール で おねがい します。
cards.example_meaning: Please apply by phone or by email.

cards.scene: p.16 — The broadcast opens: 'morning announcements from 糸守町'.
cards.context: From 知らせる (to inform). お知らせ is the standard word on notices, websites and PA systems: 本日のお知らせ (today's notices). Without お, 知らせ can also mean a sign or omen (虫の知らせ = a premonition).
cards.example_sentence: 学校からのお知らせを、親に見せるのを忘れていた。
cards.example_reading: がっこう から の おしらせ を、 おや に みせる の を わすれて いた。
cards.example_meaning: I forgot to show my parents the notice from school.

cards.scene: p.16 — The announcement is read out slowly over the speakers.
cards.context: 読む + 上げる (up, out loud). Used for lists, names, results and announcements: 名前を読み上げる (call out names). The book uses the passive 読み上げられる. It can also mean to finish reading something.
cards.example_sentence: 卒業式で、校長先生が一人一人の名前を読み上げた。
cards.example_reading: そつぎょうしき で、 こうちょう せんせい が ひとり ひとり の なまえ を よみあげた。
cards.example_meaning: At the graduation ceremony, the head teacher read out each student's name.

cards.scene: p.16 — Speakers are installed outdoors all over town, not just in homes.
cards.context: Read おくがい — 屋 is おく here, not や. Opposite: 屋内 (おくない, indoors). Common on signs and in news: 屋外プール (outdoor pool), 屋外イベント.
cards.example_sentence: 雨のため、屋外のイベントは中止になった。
cards.example_reading: あめ の ため、 おくがい の イベント は ちゅうし に なった。
cards.example_meaning: The outdoor event was cancelled because of rain.

cards.scene: p.16 — The echoing voices overlap one on top of another.
cards.context: Intransitive (重ねる is transitive). Sounds or images overlap: 声が重なる; things pile up: 仕事が重なる; dates clash: 予定が重なる (two plans fall on the same day).
cards.example_sentence: 誕生日とテストの日が重なってしまった。
cards.example_reading: たんじょうび と テスト の ひ が かさなって しまった。
cards.example_meaning: My birthday ended up on the same day as the test.

cards.scene: p.16 — The broadcast announces things like the schedule for sports day.
cards.context: A big event at Japanese schools and in small communities, usually in autumn: relay races, tug-of-war (綱引き), families picnicking. 運動 (exercise) + 会 (gathering).
cards.example_sentence: 雨で、運動会は来週に延期された。
cards.example_reading: あめ で、 うんどうかい は らいしゅう に えんき された。
cards.example_meaning: Sports day was postponed to next week because of rain.

cards.scene: p.16 — Event schedules, like the dates for sports day, go out over the speakers.
cards.context: 日程 is the dates or timetable of an event or trip: 試合の日程, 旅行の日程. 予定 is more a personal plan; スケジュール covers both. 日程を決める / 日程が変わる.
cards.example_sentence: 修学旅行の日程が、やっと決まった。
cards.example_reading: しゅうがく りょこう の にってい が、 やっと きまった。
cards.example_meaning: The dates for the school trip have finally been decided.

cards.scene: p.16 — In winter the broadcast tells people whose turn it is to shovel snow.
cards.context: 雪 + かく (掻く, to scrape, rake); also written 雪掻き. 雪かきをする. Part of everyday life in snowy mountain towns like 糸守 (modelled on 岐阜's 飛騨 area). Related: 除雪 (じょせつ, snow clearance, often by machine).
cards.example_sentence: 大雪の翌朝は、家族みんなで雪かきをした。
cards.example_reading: おおゆき の よくあさ は、 かぞく みんな で ゆきかき を した。
cards.example_meaning: The morning after the heavy snowfall, the whole family shovelled snow.

cards.scene: p.16 — The broadcast passes on messages about the snow-shovelling rota.
cards.context: A rotating duty: 掃除当番 (cleaning duty), 給食当番 (school-lunch duty); 今日は私が当番だ = it's my turn today. Compare 係 (かかり, a fixed role) and 順番 (order, turn).
cards.example_sentence: 今週は私がトイレ掃除の当番だ。
cards.example_reading: こんしゅう は わたし が トイレ そうじ の とうばん だ。
cards.example_meaning: This week it's my turn to clean the toilets.

cards.scene: p.16 — An announcement begins about the mayoral election on the 20th of next month.
cards.context: Irregular reading はつか, like 二十歳 (はたち, twenty years old). Other irregular dates: 一日 ついたち, 二日 ふつか, 八日 ようか, 十日 とおか. The book: 来月二十日 (らいげつ はつか).
cards.example_sentence: 給料は毎月二十日に振り込まれる。
cards.example_reading: きゅうりょう は まいつき はつか に ふりこまれる。
cards.example_meaning: My salary is paid into my account on the 20th of every month.

cards.scene: p.16 — The announcer starts talking about the mayoral election to be held next month.
cards.context: Passive of 行う (おこなう, to carry out). Standard in announcements and news: 選挙が行われる, 式が行われる. Watch the kana endings: 行われる (おこなわれる) vs 行かれる (いかれる, honorific of 行く).
cards.example_sentence: 今年の夏祭りは、八月の第一土曜日に行われる。
cards.example_reading: ことし の なつまつり は、 はちがつ の だいいち どようび に おこなわれる。
cards.example_meaning: This year's summer festival will be held on the first Saturday of August.

cards.scene: p.16 — The speaker is out of reach, so grandmother pulls the plug instead.
cards.context: Literal: 棚の上に手が届かない (can't reach the top shelf). Figurative: 手が届く値段 (an affordable price), 手が届かない夢 (an unreachable dream). The book adds 故に (ゆえに), a literary 'because, therefore'.
cards.example_sentence: 背が低いので、棚の一番上には手が届かない。
cards.example_reading: せ が ひくい ので、 たな の いちばん うえ に は て が とどかない。
cards.example_meaning: I'm short, so I can't reach the top shelf.

cards.scene: p.16 — Grandmother cuts off the announcement by pulling the plug out of the socket.
cards.context: コンセントを抜く = to unplug (コンセント = power socket). Many uses: 歯を抜く (pull a tooth), 力を抜く (relax), 朝ご飯を抜く (skip breakfast), 追い抜く (overtake). Intransitive: 抜ける (to come out).
cards.example_sentence: 出かける前に、アイロンのコンセントを抜いた。
cards.example_reading: でかける まえ に、 アイロン の コンセント を ぬいた。
cards.example_meaning: I unplugged the iron before going out.

cards.scene: p.16 — 三葉 picks up the remote and switches on the TV.
cards.context: 電源を入れる = to turn on; 電源を切る = to turn off; 電源が入らない = it won't power on. Also the supply or socket itself: 電源のあるカフェ (a café with plug sockets).
cards.example_sentence: 授業中は、スマホの電源を切っておきなさい。
cards.example_reading: じゅぎょうちゅう は、 スマホ の でんげん を きって おきなさい。
cards.example_meaning: Keep your phone switched off during class.

cards.scene: p.16 — On the TV, the NHK announcer starts speaking with a pleasant smile.
cards.context: な-adjective from にこにこ: にこやかな顔, にこやかに話す / 迎える. More polished and composed than にこにこ — just right for a newsreader or a hotel receptionist. Contrast にやにや (smirking) back on p.15.
cards.example_sentence: ホテルの受付の人が、にこやかに迎えてくれた。
cards.example_reading: ホテル の うけつけ の ひと が、 にこやか に むかえて くれた。
cards.example_meaning: The hotel receptionist greeted us with a warm smile.

cards.scene: p.17 — TV news: the comet's arrival is now a month away.
cards.context: Something urgent or threatening coming closer: 危険が迫る, 締め切りが迫る (a deadline looms), 時間が迫る. 近づく is neutral 'get closer'; 迫る feels pressing. 返事を迫る = to press someone for an answer.
cards.example_sentence: 試験が三日後に迫って、毎日図書館で勉強している。
cards.example_reading: しけん が みっかご に せまって、 まいにち としょかん で べんきょう して いる。
cards.example_meaning: The exam is only three days away, so I'm studying in the library every day.

cards.scene: p.17 — the TV screen shows a caption about the comet.
cards.context: 画 (picture) + 面 (surface). スマホの画面 / テレビの画面. 画面が割れる = the screen cracks; 待ち受け画面 = home-screen picture.
cards.example_sentence: スマホの画面が割れてしまった。
cards.example_reading: スマホ の がめん が われて しまった。
cards.example_meaning: My smartphone screen got cracked.

cards.scene: p.17 — the sisters go down the stone-wall steps.
cards.context: 階段を上る (のぼる) / 下りる (おりる); 一段 = one step. Stone shrine steps are 石段 (Ch.1 deck); 階段 is the everyday word for any stairs.
cards.example_sentence: 階段を一段ずつゆっくり上った。
cards.example_reading: かいだん を いちだん ずつ ゆっくり のぼった。
cards.example_meaning: I went up the stairs slowly, one step at a time.

cards.scene: p.17 — The news says the comet is now, at last, just a month away (いよいよ…迫っています).
cards.context: Used when something long awaited (or feared) is finally close: いよいよ明日だ！ = 'Tomorrow's the day!' Often goes with 迫る (draw near) or 始まる. やっと = finally, with relief once it has happened; ついに = at last, as the end result.
cards.example_sentence: 来週からいよいよ夏休みだ。
cards.example_reading: らいしゅう から いよいよ なつやすみ だ。
cards.example_meaning: Summer vacation finally starts next week.

meanings: of the century (once in an era)
cards.scene: p.17 — The newsreader calls the comet 'the celestial show of the century' (世紀の天体ショー).
cards.context: 世紀 = a numbered century: 二十一世紀 (the 21st century). 世紀の + noun = 'of the century', once in an era: 世紀の大発見 (discovery of the century). For any span of 100 years, say 百年.
cards.example_sentence: このお寺は十二世紀に建てられたそうだ。
cards.example_reading: この おてら は じゅうにせいき に たてられた そう だ。
cards.example_meaning: They say this temple was built in the 12th century.

cards.scene: p.17 — The TV screen shows a caption: Comet Tiamat, visible to the naked eye in a month (〜の文字).
cards.context: Written characters or letters: ひらがなは日本の文字です. On a screen, 〜の文字 means 'the words ~', a caption or headline. 字 (じ) alone is one character, or someone's handwriting (字がきれい).
cards.example_sentence: 黒板の文字が小さくて、後ろの席からは読めない。
cards.example_reading: こくばん の もじ が ちいさくて、 うしろ の せき から は よめない。
cards.example_meaning: The writing on the blackboard is so small I can't read it from the back.

cards.scene: p.17 — Next to the caption, blurry footage of the comet (ぼやけた彗星の映像) plays on the TV.
cards.context: Moving pictures or images on a screen: ニュースの映像, 映像がきれい (the picture is sharp). 画像 (がぞう) is a still image such as a photo file; 映画 (えいが) is a film. 映 (project, as in 映る) + 像 (image, statue).
cards.example_sentence: このテレビは古いけど、映像はまだきれいだ。
cards.example_reading: この テレビ は ふるい けど、 えいぞう は まだ きれい だ。
cards.example_meaning: This TV is old, but the picture is still clear.

cards.scene: p.17 — After the news report, the conversation at the table somehow just dies out.
cards.context: Without a clear reason, just a vague feeling: なんとなく分かる (I sort of get it), なんとなく気まずい (it's kind of awkward). Kanji form 何となく. Close to なぜか (for some reason), but なんとなく puts more weight on how vague your own feeling is.
cards.example_sentence: 今日はなんとなく、だれとも話したくない。
cards.example_reading: きょう は なんとなく、 だれ とも はなしたく ない。
cards.example_meaning: For some reason I just don't feel like talking to anyone today.

cards.scene: p.17 — Mixed in with the NHK broadcast, the only other sound is the three of them eating.
cards.context: Intransitive: something gets mixed in among other things, as in 雨に雪が混じる (sleet) or 声に笑いが混じる. The transitive partner is 混ぜる (まぜる, to mix something). 混ざる means almost the same; 混じる is a little more for things you can still pick out, like sounds, colours or hair.
cards.example_sentence: 彼女の黒い髪には、少し白い髪が混じっていた。
cards.example_reading: かのじょ の くろい かみ に は、 すこし しろい かみ が まじって いた。
cards.example_meaning: There were a few white hairs mixed in with her black hair.

cards.scene: p.17 — The only sounds at the table are eating noises, as quiet as whispering.
cards.context: ひそひそ話す = to whisper so others can't hear; ひそひそ話 = a whispered conversation, often gossip. Compare ぶつぶつ (muttering complaints to yourself) and こそこそ (doing something sneakily).
cards.example_sentence: 後ろの席の二人が、ずっとひそひそ話している。
cards.example_reading: うしろ の せき の ふたり が、 ずっと ひそひそ はなして いる。
cards.example_meaning: The two people in the seats behind me keep whispering.

cards.scene: p.17 — 四葉 suddenly tells them to make up already (いいかげん、仲直り…), meaning grandma and the girls' father.
cards.context: Three uses: (1) adverb, いいかげん〜しなさい = 'it's about time you ~', impatient; (2) な-adjective, いいかげんな人 = a sloppy, irresponsible person; (3) いいかげんにして！ = 'cut it out!' Kanji form いい加減, literally 'a good amount'.
cards.example_sentence: もう夜中だよ。いいかげん寝なさい。
cards.example_reading: もう よなか だ よ。 いいかげん ねなさい。
cards.example_meaning: It's the middle of the night. Go to sleep already.

cards.scene: p.17 — 四葉 urges the grown-ups to make up: grandma and the girls' father have fallen out.
cards.context: 仲 (relationship, as in 仲がいい) + 直り (from 直る, to get fixed): mending a relationship after a fight. 〜と仲直りする = to make up with ~. The opposite is けんかする or 仲が悪くなる.
cards.example_sentence: きのうけんかした友達と、今日やっと仲直りした。
cards.example_reading: きのう けんか した ともだち と、 きょう やっと なかなおり した。
cards.example_meaning: Today I finally made up with the friend I fought with yesterday.

meanings: to pick up on what's unsaid
cards.scene: p.17 — 四葉 makes a remark that completely fails to read the room (空気を読まない発言).
cards.context: Literally 'to read the air': to sense what people feel without being told and act to fit it, an important social skill in Japan. 空気が読めない人 = someone who keeps missing the mood. 空気 here means the atmosphere in a room, like 雰囲気.
cards.example_sentence: 会議中に冗談を言うなんて、彼は空気が読めないね。
cards.example_reading: かいぎちゅう に じょうだん を いう なんて、 かれ は くうき が よめない ね。
cards.example_meaning: Cracking a joke in the middle of a meeting? He really can't read the room.

cards.scene: p.17 — 四葉's tactless remark about the family feud makes 三葉 snap back.
cards.context: A remark or statement, especially in front of a group: 発言する (to speak up), 問題発言 (a controversial remark), 失言 (しつげん, a slip of the tongue). More formal than 言ったこと.
cards.example_sentence: 授業中、彼女はいつも積極的に発言する。
cards.example_reading: じゅぎょうちゅう、 かのじょ は いつも せっきょくてき に はつげん する。
cards.example_meaning: She always speaks up eagerly in class.

cards.scene: p.17 — The sisters call out 'I'm off!' together to grandma as they leave.
cards.context: Written-register 'tell' or 'announce': 別れを告げる (to say goodbye), 名前を告げる, 時を告げる鐘 (a bell that tolls the hour). In speech you'd use 言う or 伝える. Related words: 報告 (ほうこく, report) and 告白 (こくはく, confession).
cards.example_sentence: 駅員が、電車が遅れていることを乗客に告げた。
cards.example_reading: えきいん が、 でんしゃ が おくれて いる こと を じょうきゃく に つげた。
cards.example_meaning: The station attendant told the passengers that the train was delayed.

cards.scene: p.17 — 三葉 and 四葉 head out through the front door of the house.
cards.context: The entry area of a Japanese house, a step lower than the floor, where you take off your shoes. 玄関を出る = to leave the house; 玄関で靴を脱ぐ = to take off your shoes at the door. A large building's main entrance is its 正面玄関.
cards.example_sentence: 玄関で靴を脱いでから、上がってください。
cards.example_reading: げんかん で くつ を ぬいで から、 あがって ください。
cards.example_meaning: Please take off your shoes in the entryway before you come in.

cards.scene: p.18 — the round lake 糸守湖 shining below them.
cards.context: On its own it's みずうみ; in names it's 〜湖 (こ): 琵琶湖 (びわこ), 糸守湖 (いともりこ).
cards.example_sentence: 湖の水面に、夕日が映っていた。
cards.example_reading: みずうみ の すいめん に、 ゆうひ が うつって いた。
cards.example_meaning: The evening sun was reflected on the surface of the lake.

cards.scene: p.18 — she jokes about herself: a high-school girl with dazzling bare legs.
cards.context: The book writes it in kanji with furigana (眩しい). Light so bright you can't look straight at it: 日差しがまぶしい. Figurative: まぶしい笑顔 = a radiant smile. The kanji 眩しい is usually written in kana.
cards.example_sentence: 朝の日差しがまぶしくて、目を細めた。
cards.example_reading: あさ の ひざし が まぶしくて、 め を ほそめた。
cards.example_meaning: The morning sun was so bright that I squinted.

cards.scene: p.18 — someone calls out to her back.
cards.context: 背 alone can also mean height (背が高い). 背中を向ける = to turn your back; 背中を押す = to give someone a push, encourage them.
cards.example_sentence: 父の大きな背中を見て育った。
cards.example_reading: ちち の おおきな せなか を みて そだった。
cards.example_meaning: I grew up watching my father's broad back.

cards.scene: p.18 — her friends call out to her (背中に声をかけられた).
cards.context: 〜に声をかける = to speak to someone to start a conversation, invite them, or check they're OK. 話しかける is similar; 声をかける is lighter — a greeting or a first word.
cards.example_sentence: 道に迷っていたら、おばあさんが声をかけてくれた。
cards.example_reading: みち に まよって いたら、 おばあさん が こえ を かけて くれた。
cards.example_meaning: When I was lost, an old woman spoke to me.

cards.scene: p.18 — after parting from 四葉 at the primary school.
cards.context: 〜と別れる = to part from someone; also to break up with a partner. 分かれる (same sound) is for something splitting: 道が分かれる. Noun: 別れ = a parting, a farewell.
cards.example_sentence: 駅で友達と別れて、一人で家に帰った。
cards.example_reading: えき で ともだち と わかれて、 ひとり で いえ に かえった。
cards.example_meaning: I said goodbye to my friend at the station and went home alone.

cards.scene: p.18 — 「仲いいなあ」: you two get on so well.
cards.context: 仲がいい = to be close, get along; 仲良くなる = to become friends; 仲直りする = to make up after a fight. 仲間 (なかま) = friends, teammates.
cards.example_sentence: 最初はけんかばかりしていたが、今ではすっかり仲良くなった。
cards.example_reading: さいしょ は けんか ばかり して いた が、 いま で は すっかり なかよく なった。
cards.example_meaning: At first we fought all the time, but now we've become really close.

cards.scene: p.18 — their earnest denial makes her giggle.
cards.context: 真剣な顔 = a serious face; 真剣に考える = to think hard about something. まじめ is a personality (diligent, sincere); 真剣 is how focused you are right now. 本気 = you really mean it.
cards.example_sentence: 先生は私の相談を、真剣に聞いてくれた。
cards.example_reading: せんせい は わたし の そうだん を、 しんけん に きいて くれた。
cards.example_meaning: My teacher listened seriously to my problem.

cards.scene: p.18 — The calm surface of the lake shines in the sun.
cards.context: Usually read すいめん; the poetic readings are みなも and みずも. 水面に映る (to be reflected on the water), 水面に浮かぶ (to float on the surface). 海面 (かいめん) is the surface of the sea.
cards.example_sentence: 池の水面に、月がきれいに映っている。
cards.example_reading: いけ の すいめん に、 つき が きれい に うつって いる。
cards.example_meaning: The moon is reflected beautifully on the surface of the pond.

cards.scene: p.18 — 三葉 casts herself as the bare-legged high-school girl in the opening shot of a Japanese film.
cards.context: Short for 女子高校生: 女子 (girl, female) + 高生 (from 高校生). Related words: 男子高生 (high-school boy), 女子大生 (female university student). 女子高 (じょしこう) alone means a girls' high school.
cards.example_sentence: 駅前のカフェは、いつも女子高生でいっぱいだ。
cards.example_reading: えきまえ の カフェ は、 いつも じょしこうせい で いっぱい だ。
cards.example_meaning: The café in front of the station is always full of high-school girls.

cards.scene: p.18 — After her movie daydream, 三葉 sums it up: in short, they live out in the old-fashioned Japanese sticks.
cards.context: Kanji form 要するに (要 = the main point). Sums up what came before: 要するに、お金がないってこと？ Close to つまり, but ようするに can sound blunt or impatient. The book pairs it with ど田舎 (どいなか), an emphatic 'the middle of nowhere'.
cards.example_sentence: 長い話だったけど、ようするに彼は来られないということだ。
cards.example_reading: ながい はなし だった けど、 ようするに かれ は こられない という こと だ。
cards.example_meaning: It was a long story, but basically he can't come.

cards.scene: p.18 — テッシー pedals his bike looking grumpy, with サヤちん riding on the back.
cards.context: 不 (not) + 機嫌 (mood, temper): 不機嫌な顔 (a sour face), 不機嫌そう (looking grumpy). Opposite: 上機嫌 (じょうきげん, in high spirits). In everyday talk, 機嫌がいい / 機嫌が悪い.
cards.example_sentence: 寝不足の父は、朝から不機嫌だった。
cards.example_reading: ねぶそく の ちち は、 あさ から ふきげん だった。
cards.example_meaning: My dad hadn't had enough sleep and was grumpy from the morning on.

meanings: to sit (on a chair, edge, ledge)
cards.scene: p.18 — サヤちん sits small and neat (ちょこんと腰掛けて) on the bike's rack, all smiles.
cards.context: 腰 (hips, lower back) + 掛ける (to hang, set): to sit on something raised, such as a chair, bench or edge, not on the floor. 座る is the general word, and the one for sitting on tatami. ちょこんと腰掛ける = to perch small and neat.
cards.example_sentence: おじいさんはベンチに腰掛けて、新聞を読んでいた。
cards.example_reading: おじいさん は ベンチ に こしかけて、 しんぶん を よんで いた。
cards.example_meaning: The old man was sitting on a bench reading the newspaper.

cards.scene: p.18 — テッシー grumbles at サヤちん to get off his bike.
cards.context: ぶつぶつ言う = to grumble or mutter to yourself, usually complaints: 文句をぶつぶつ言う. It can also describe bumps or spots on skin (顔にぶつぶつができた). Compare ひそひそ (whispering to someone) and ぼそぼそ (mumbling quietly).
cards.example_sentence: 弟は宿題をしながら、ずっとぶつぶつ文句を言っている。
cards.example_reading: おとうと は しゅくだい を しながら、 ずっと ぶつぶつ もんく を いって いる。
cards.example_meaning: My little brother keeps grumbling while he does his homework.

cards.scene: p.18 — When テッシー tells her to get off, サヤちん fires back: 'Stingy!'
cards.context: Stingy, unwilling to share: ケチな人, or ケチ！ as a playful retort. Usually written in katakana (the kanji 吝嗇 is rare). ケチをつける = to find fault with something. Here it's teasing: テッシー is being 'stingy' with his bike rack.
cards.example_sentence: 一口くらいくれてもいいじゃん。ケチ！
cards.example_reading: ひとくち くらい くれて も いい じゃん。 ケチ！
cards.example_meaning: You could at least give me one bite. Stingy!

cards.scene: p.18 — The pair's dead-serious denial (真剣な否定っぷり) makes 三葉 laugh.
cards.context: 否定する = to deny or reject something: うわさを否定する. Opposite: 肯定 (こうてい, affirmation); 否定的 = negative (attitude). The book's 否定っぷり uses 〜っぷり ('the way of ~'): the way they deny it is so earnest it's funny.
cards.example_sentence: 彼はうわさをはっきり否定した。
cards.example_reading: かれ は うわさ を はっきり ひてい した。
cards.example_meaning: He flatly denied the rumour.

cards.scene: p.18 — 三葉 can't help giggling at her friends' bickering.
cards.context: くすくす笑う = to giggle softly while trying to hold it in. Compare げらげら (loud guffaws), にこにこ (smiling) and にやにや (smirking, a knowing grin).
cards.example_sentence: 先生の寝ぐせを見て、生徒たちはくすくす笑った。
cards.example_reading: せんせい の ねぐせ を みて、 せいとたち は くすくす わらった。
cards.example_meaning: Seeing the teacher's bedhead, the students giggled.

cards.scene: p.19 — she always wears the same hairstyle, the one her mother taught her.
cards.context: 髪型を変える = to change your hairstyle; also ヘアスタイル. 〜型 = shape or type (血液型 = blood type).
cards.example_sentence: 髪型を変えたら、友だちに気づいてもらえなかった。
cards.example_reading: かみがた を かえたら、 ともだち に きづいて もらえなかった。
cards.example_meaning: When I changed my hairstyle, my friends didn't even notice.

cards.scene: p.19 — サヤちん touches 三葉's hair cord.
cards.context: Both 〜に触る and 〜を触る are used. 触れる (ふれる) is softer and more written (a light touch, or touching on a topic). Signs say 触らないでください = please don't touch.
cards.example_sentence: 熱いから、なべに触らないで。
cards.example_reading: あつい から、 なべ に さわらないで。
cards.example_meaning: Don't touch the pot. It's hot.

cards.scene: p.19 — テッシー: it was definitely fox possession!
cards.context: 絶対に〜ない = never, under any circumstances: 絶対に見ないで. Positive: 絶対に行く (I'll definitely go). 必ず works for positive sentences only; 絶対 works for both. テッシー says it in katakana: ゼッタイ.
cards.example_sentence: このことは、絶対にだれにも言わないで。
cards.example_reading: この こと は、 ぜったい に だれ に も いわないで。
cards.example_meaning: Never tell anyone about this.

cards.scene: p.19 — テッシー's shaven head is described as a bit uncool (book: ダサめ).
cards.context: Casual slang for uncool or tacky: ダサい服, ダサいな. The opposite is かっこいい or おしゃれ. The book's ダサめ uses 〜め ('on the ~ side'), as in 大きめ and 早め, so 'a bit uncool'.
cards.example_sentence: その服、ちょっとダサくない？
cards.example_reading: その ふく、 ちょっと ださく ない？
cards.example_meaning: Isn't that outfit a bit uncool?

cards.scene: p.19 — 三葉 secretly thinks the bickering pair actually suit each other.
cards.context: Noun / な-adjective from 似合う (to suit): お似合いのカップル (a well-matched couple), 二人はお似合いだ. It can also be sarcastic: あんたにはそれがお似合いよ ('that's just what you deserve').
cards.example_sentence: あの二人、性格は正反対だけど、意外とお似合いだと思う。
cards.example_reading: あの ふたり、 せいかく は せいはんたい だ けど、 いがいと おにあい だ と おもう。
cards.example_meaning: Those two have opposite personalities, but I think they're a surprisingly good match.

cards.scene: p.19 — 三葉 wears a braid on each side, wound up and tied behind her head.
cards.context: Left and right: 左右を見る (look both ways), 左右対称 (symmetrical). As a verb, 左右する means 'to sway, decide': 天気に左右される (to depend on the weather). Same pattern: 前後 (front and back), 上下 (up and down).
cards.example_sentence: 道を渡る前に、左右をよく見なさい。
cards.example_reading: みち を わたる まえ に、 さゆう を よく みなさい。
cards.example_meaning: Look carefully left and right before you cross the road.

cards.scene: p.19 — 三葉's two braids are wound around and tied with her cord, a style her mother taught her.
cards.context: 三つ (three) + 編み (from 編む, to braid, knit): a three-strand braid. 三つ編みにする = to braid your hair. Related: 編み物 (knitting) and 組紐 (braided cord), which also weaves strands together.
cards.example_sentence: 妹は毎朝、母に三つ編みをしてもらっている。
cards.example_reading: いもうと は まいあさ、 はは に みつあみ を して もらって いる。
cards.example_meaning: Every morning my little sister has our mother braid her hair.

cards.scene: p.19 — 三葉's braids are coiled around (くるりと巻いて) and tied at the back of her head.
cards.context: To wind or wrap something around: マフラーを巻く (to wrap a scarf), 包帯を巻く (to put on a bandage), くるりと巻く (to coil around once). Intransitive: 巻きつく (to coil around). 巻 is also the counter for volumes (第一巻).
cards.example_sentence: 寒いので、首にマフラーを巻いて出かけた。
cards.example_reading: さむい ので、 くび に マフラー を まいて でかけた。
cards.example_meaning: It was cold, so I wrapped a scarf around my neck before going out.

cards.scene: p.19 — サヤちん's remark about her hair reminds 三葉 of the half-finished conversation at breakfast.
cards.context: そう言えば = 'speaking of that, now that you mention it', used when something reminds you of something else. Often shortened to そういや in speech. ところで (by the way) changes the topic without any link.
cards.example_sentence: そういえば、昨日借りた本をまだ返していなかった。
cards.example_reading: そういえば、 きのう かりた ほん を まだ かえして いなかった。
cards.example_meaning: Come to think of it, I still haven't returned the book I borrowed yesterday.

cards.scene: p.19 — 三葉 recalls the breakfast conversation that was left hanging.
cards.context: The written or formal word for 朝ごはん: 朝食付き (breakfast included) on hotel plans. Same set: 昼食 (ちゅうしょく, lunch), 夕食 (ゆうしょく, dinner). 朝 is read ちょう in compounds, as in 朝刊 and 早朝.
cards.example_sentence: このホテルは朝食付きで一泊八千円だ。
cards.example_reading: この ホテル は ちょうしょくつき で いっぱく はっせんえん だ。
cards.example_meaning: This hotel is 8,000 yen a night with breakfast included.

cards.scene: p.19 — サヤちん insists 三葉 is just stressed out (ストレス溜まっとるんよ, in dialect).
cards.context: Intransitive たまる (to build up) vs transitive ためる (to save up, let build up): ストレスがたまる, 宿題がたまる, お金をためる. 溜 isn't a standard school kanji, so you'll often see it in kana; 貯まる is used for money. サヤちん's 溜まっとる is dialect for 溜まっている.
cards.example_sentence: 最近忙しくて、ストレスが溜まっている。
cards.example_reading: さいきん いそがしくて、 ストレス が たまって いる。
cards.example_meaning: I've been busy lately, and the stress is building up.

cards.scene: p.20 — her father, tall and imposing in manner.
cards.context: 態度がいい / 悪い = a good / bad attitude; 態度が大きい = acting big, arrogant; 態度を変える = to change how you act towards someone.
cards.example_sentence: 先生に注意されて、彼は急に態度を変えた。
cards.example_reading: せんせい に ちゅうい されて、 かれ は きゅう に たいど を かえた。
cards.example_meaning: After the teacher warned him, he suddenly changed his attitude.

meanings: on the spur of the moment
cards.scene: p.20 — Asked about yesterday, 三葉 can't recall it on the spot; it must have been an ordinary day… surely?
cards.context: Kanji 咄嗟 (rarely written). とっさに = instantly, with no time to think: a reflex (とっさに手を出す, とっさに嘘をつく), or with a negative, とっさには思い出せない = 'can't come up with it right away'. The は adds contrast: not right now, though maybe later.
cards.example_sentence: ボールが飛んできて、とっさに目を閉じた。
cards.example_reading: ボール が とんで きて、 とっさに め を とじた。
cards.example_meaning: A ball came flying at me and I shut my eyes on reflex.

cards.scene: p.20 — 三葉 wonders why everyone (grandma, 四葉, now her friends) is worried about her all at once.
cards.context: From 揃う (そろう, to be all present / to match). The te-form works as an adverb: 家族そろって (the whole family together), 二人そろって (both of them, alike). On p.15 she already grumbles that 四葉 and grandma are 二人そろって rude. Usually written in kana.
cards.example_sentence: お正月には家族そろって神社にお参りに行く。
cards.example_reading: おしょうがつ に は かぞく そろって じんじゃ に おまいり に いく。
cards.example_meaning: At New Year the whole family goes to the shrine together.

cards.scene: p.20 — A gruff megaphone voice cuts in and wipes 三葉's question about yesterday out of her head.
cards.context: 疑問 is a question you hold in your mind (a doubt, a 'why?'); 質問 is a question you put to someone. 疑問に思う = to wonder about, find questionable; 疑問を持つ = to have doubts; 疑問文 = a question sentence. 疑 = doubt, as in 疑う (うたがう).
cards.example_sentence: 先生の説明を聞いて、新しい疑問がわいてきた。
cards.example_reading: せんせい の せつめい を きいて、 あたらしい ぎもん が わいて きた。
cards.example_meaning: Listening to the teacher's explanation, a new question came to mind.

cards.scene: p.20 — The car park sits across from the greenhouses.
cards.context: Nの向かい側 = across from N, facing it: 駅の向かい側 (across from the station), 道の向かい側 (across the road). 向かい alone works too: 向かいの家 (the house opposite). 反対側 just means the other side, not necessarily facing.
cards.example_sentence: 郵便局は銀行の向かい側にあります。
cards.example_reading: ゆうびんきょく は ぎんこう の むかいがわ に あります。
cards.example_meaning: The post office is across from the bank.

cards.scene: p.20 — The speech is held in the town-run car park (町営駐車場), the only big open space around.
cards.context: 駐 (stop, stay) + 車 + 場 (place). 駐車 = parking; 駐車禁止 = no parking; 駐輪場 (ちゅうりんじょう) = bicycle parking. 町営 (ちょうえい) = run by the town, like 市営 (city-run).
cards.example_sentence: コンビニの駐車場で友だちと待ち合わせた。
cards.example_reading: コンビニ の ちゅうしゃじょう で ともだち と まちあわせた。
cards.example_meaning: I met my friend in the convenience store car park.

cards.scene: p.20 — 三葉 calls the town car park pointlessly big (無駄に広い): a lot of tarmac for a town of 1,500.
cards.context: な-adjective / noun: 無駄な時間 (wasted time), 無駄遣い (wasting money), 無駄にする (to waste). 無駄に + adjective is a sarcastic favourite in young people's speech: 無駄に広い, 無駄に高い = 'needlessly big / pricey'. 駄 is the same kanji as in 駄目 (だめ).
cards.example_sentence: あの店は無駄に高いから、もう行かない。
cards.example_reading: あの みせ は むだに たかい から、 もう いかない。
cards.example_meaning: That shop is needlessly expensive, so I'm not going any more.

cards.scene: p.20 — In the middle of the little crowd, microphone in hand, stands 三葉's father.
cards.context: その中心で = in the middle of it. 中心 is also abstract: 話の中心 (the heart of the matter), 町の中心 (town centre), 〜を中心に (centred on ~). 真ん中 is more physical and everyday.
cards.example_sentence: この町は駅を中心に広がっている。
cards.example_reading: この まち は えき を ちゅうしん に ひろがって いる。
cards.example_meaning: This town spreads out around the station.

cards.scene: p.20 — Her father has an imposing, self-assured manner as he addresses the crowd.
cards.context: 堂々と / 堂々とした: confident and dignified, with nothing to hide: 堂々と話す, 堂々とした態度, 正々堂々 (fair and square). 々 repeats the kanji (堂堂). Usually admiring, but 三葉's description has an edge: on p.21 the same confidence feels overbearing (高圧的).
cards.example_sentence: 初めての発表だったが、彼女は堂々と話した。
cards.example_reading: はじめて の はっぴょう だった が、 かのじょ は どうどう と はなした。
cards.example_meaning: It was her first presentation, but she spoke with confidence.

cards.scene: p.21 — his speech sounds like a politician (政治家) on TV.
cards.context: 政治家 (せいじか) = politician; 政治的 = political.
cards.example_sentence: 父は若い頃から政治に興味があった。
cards.example_reading: ちち は わかい ころ から せいじ に きょうみ が あった。
cards.example_meaning: My father has been interested in politics since he was young.

cards.scene: p.21 — 'a community where everyone, young and old, can play an active part'.
cards.context: 活躍する = to do great things, be the star: 試合で活躍する, 世界で活躍する選手. 大活躍 = a brilliant performance. 躍 (leap) is a hard kanji; this is the word to learn it from.
cards.example_sentence: 新しい選手の大活躍で、チームは試合に勝った。
cards.example_reading: あたらしい せんしゅ の だいかつやく で、 チーム は しあい に かった。
cards.example_meaning: Thanks to the new player's brilliant performance, the team won the match.

meanings: to achieve, come true (実現する)
cards.scene: p.21 — Her father lays out his plans: once sound finances are achieved, he will make a lively community a reality.
cards.context: 実現する = to realise, bring about (a plan, dream, promise); 実現させる is also common. 夢が実現する = a dream comes true (like 夢がかなう). Politicians love it: 〜を実現します. 実 (real) + 現 (appear).
cards.example_sentence: 長年の夢がついに実現して、彼は自分の店を開いた。
cards.example_reading: ながねん の ゆめ が ついに じつげん して、 かれ は じぶん の みせ を ひらいた。
cards.example_meaning: His long-held dream finally came true, and he opened his own shop.

cards.simpler_synonym: おじいさん・おばあさん
cards.scene: p.21 — The mayor promises a community where everyone, from children to the elderly, can live with peace of mind.
cards.context: The kind, polite word for elderly people: 老人 (ろうじん) sounds cold and clinical, 高齢者 (こうれいしゃ) is official. 子どもからお年寄りまで = from kids to seniors, i.e. everyone. Rural towns like 糸守 have many お年寄り.
cards.example_sentence: 電車でお年寄りに席をゆずった。
cards.example_reading: でんしゃ で おとしより に せき を ゆずった。
cards.example_meaning: I gave up my seat to an elderly person on the train.

cards.scene: p.21 — He pledges a community where everyone can be active and lively, young and old alike.
cards.context: Usually written 生き生き; the book uses 活き活き (活 = active, as in 活躍 かつやく). いきいきと + verb: いきいきと働く; いきいきした表情 (a lively face). A doubled mimetic word like わくわく, from the root of 生きる: literally 'alive-alive'.
cards.example_sentence: 新しい仕事を始めてから、姉は毎日活き活きしている。
cards.example_reading: あたらしい しごと を はじめて から、 あね は まいにち いきいき して いる。
cards.example_meaning: Since starting her new job, my sister has been full of life every day.

cards.scene: p.21 — The slick speech feels out of place in a car park surrounded by fields.
cards.context: 畑 is a dry field for vegetables and other crops; 田んぼ (たんぼ) / 田 is a flooded rice paddy. 畑仕事 = farm work. A kanji made in Japan: 火 + 田, fields cleared by burning.
cards.example_sentence: 祖母は家の裏の畑でトマトやなすを育てている。
cards.example_reading: そぼ は いえ の うら の はたけ で トマト や なす を そだてて いる。
cards.example_meaning: My grandmother grows tomatoes and aubergines in the field behind the house.

cards.scene: p.21 — The car park is hemmed in by fields (畑に囲まれた).
cards.context: Passive 〜に囲まれる = to be surrounded by: 山に囲まれた町 (a town ringed by mountains, just like 糸守). Also 食卓を囲む (gather round the table), 丸で囲む (circle an answer). Related nouns: 周囲 (しゅうい), 囲い (かこい, an enclosure).
cards.example_sentence: 正しい答えを丸で囲んでください。
cards.example_reading: ただしい こたえ を まる で かこんで ください。
cards.example_meaning: Please circle the correct answer.

cards.scene: p.21 — Listeners mutter that he'll win again this term anyway (どうせ今期も).
cards.context: どうせ adds resignation or cynicism: 'it will turn out that way no matter what'. どうせ無理だ (it's hopeless anyway), どうせなら (if we're doing it anyway, then…). Often paired with a guess: どうせ〜だろう / 〜やろ. Contrast せっかく (since we went to the trouble), which is positive.
cards.example_sentence: どうせ遅刻するなら、ゆっくり朝ごはんを食べよう。
cards.example_reading: どうせ ちこく する なら、 ゆっくり あさごはん を たべよう。
cards.example_meaning: If I'm going to be late anyway, I might as well enjoy my breakfast.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book (expected later in Ch.2): Getting dressed for school in her uniform.
cards.context: 制 (rule) + 服 (clothes). 私服 (しふく) = your own clothes. セーラー服 = sailor-style school uniform.
cards.example_sentence: うちの高校の制服は、セーラー服だ。
cards.example_reading: うち の こうこう の せいふく は、 セーラーふく だ。
cards.example_meaning: Our high school's uniform is a sailor suit.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book (expected later in Ch.2): The morning routine at 三葉's house.
cards.context: 着 (wear) + 替える (switch). Noun: 着替え = a change of clothes. Also read きかえる.
cards.example_sentence: 雨でぬれたので、すぐに着替えた。
cards.example_reading: あめ で ぬれた ので、 すぐ に きがえた。
cards.example_meaning: I got wet in the rain, so I changed right away.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book (expected later in Ch.2): Fits the rushed school mornings.
cards.context: 寝坊する = to oversleep. 朝寝坊 = a late riser. Not the same as 寝不足 (ねぶそく, not enough sleep).
cards.example_sentence: 寝坊して、バスに乗り遅れた。
cards.example_reading: ねぼう して、 バス に のりおくれた。
cards.example_meaning: I overslept and missed the bus.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book (expected later in Ch.2): The mayoral election: her father is one of the candidates.
cards.context: 候補者 = a candidate (person); 立候補する = to run for office; 優勝候補 = a favourite to win.
cards.example_sentence: 今度の選挙には、三人の候補者がいる。
cards.example_reading: こんど の せんきょ に は、 さんにん の こうほしゃ が いる。
cards.example_meaning: There are three candidates in the coming election.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book (expected later in Ch.2): テッシー and サヤちん are 三葉's childhood friends.
cards.context: 幼い (young) + なじみ (familiar). Someone you've known since you were small. Also written 幼馴染.
cards.example_sentence: 彼とは幼なじみで、小さい頃からいつも一緒だった。
cards.example_reading: かれ と は おさななじみ で、 ちいさい ころ から いつも いっしょ だった。
cards.example_meaning: He's my childhood friend; we've always been together since we were little.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book (expected later in Ch.2): 三葉's classmates — some friendly, some not.
cards.context: 同 (same) + 級 (grade) + 生. 同い年 (おないどし) = the same age.
cards.example_sentence: 駅で、中学の同級生にばったり会った。
cards.example_reading: えき で、 ちゅうがく の どうきゅうせい に ばったり あった。
cards.example_meaning: I bumped into a classmate from junior high at the station.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book (expected later in Ch.2): In a small town everyone talks — the shrine family and the mayor are always gossip.
cards.context: 噂をする = to gossip about; 噂が広まる = a rumour spreads. Saying: 噂をすれば… = speak of the devil.
cards.example_sentence: 新しい先生の噂は、すぐに学校中に広まった。
cards.example_reading: あたらしい せんせい の うわさ は、 すぐ に がっこうじゅう に ひろまった。
cards.example_meaning: Rumours about the new teacher quickly spread through the school.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book (expected later in Ch.2): Classmates tease 三葉 about her family and the shrine.
cards.context: 人をからかう; passive からかわれる = to be teased. Lighter than いじめる (to bully).
cards.example_sentence: 弟はいつも私をからかって笑う。
cards.example_reading: おとうと は いつも わたし を からかって わらう。
cards.example_meaning: My little brother is always teasing me and laughing.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book (expected later in Ch.2): Her friends say she seemed strange yesterday.
cards.context: 様子がおかしい / 様子が変 = acting strangely. 様子を見る = to wait and see.
cards.example_sentence: 今日の彼は、なんだか様子が変だった。
cards.example_reading: きょう の かれ は、 なんだか ようす が へん だった。
cards.example_meaning: He seemed somehow off today.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book (expected later in Ch.2): 'You were acting strange yesterday' — the friends' first clue that something's going on.
cards.context: な-adjective: 変な人, 変な味. 変だ = something's off. Don't confuse with 大変 (たいへん, terrible / very).
cards.example_sentence: 冷蔵庫から変なにおいがする。
cards.example_reading: れいぞうこ から へんな におい が する。
cards.example_meaning: There's a strange smell coming from the fridge.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book (expected later in Ch.2): Odd things start happening to 三葉 that she can't explain.
cards.context: 不思議な usually means wondrous or puzzling (neutral or positive); 変な leans negative. 不思議に思う = to wonder about something.
cards.example_sentence: 不思議なことに、その日のことを何も覚えていない。
cards.example_reading: ふしぎな こと に、 その ひ の こと を なにも おぼえて いない。
cards.example_meaning: Strangely, I don't remember anything about that day.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book (expected later in Ch.2): The teacher writes old words for twilight on the blackboard.
cards.context: 黒 (black) + 板 (board). 黒板を消す = to erase the board.
cards.example_sentence: 先生が黒板に大きく字を書いた。
cards.example_reading: せんせい が こくばん に おおきく じ を かいた。
cards.example_meaning: The teacher wrote large characters on the blackboard.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book (expected later in Ch.2): In class, the town's own word for twilight turns out to be dialect.
cards.context: 方 (region) + 言 (speech). 標準語 (ひょうじゅんご) = standard Japanese. Named dialects use 〜弁: 関西弁, 飛騨弁 — the model for Itomori speech.
cards.example_sentence: 祖母の方言は、ときどき聞き取れない。
cards.example_reading: そぼ の ほうげん は、 ときどき ききとれない。
cards.example_meaning: Sometimes I can't catch my grandmother's dialect.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book (expected later in Ch.2): 三葉 dreams of the big city — the opposite of her small town.
cards.context: 都会 (city life) vs 田舎 (countryside). 都会的 = urban, sophisticated. 都市 (とし) is the more technical word.
cards.example_sentence: 都会の生活にあこがれて、東京に出た。
cards.example_reading: とかい の せいかつ に あこがれて、 とうきょう に でた。
cards.example_meaning: I longed for city life, so I moved to Tokyo.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book (expected later in Ch.2): To 三葉, small-town life feels dull.
cards.context: な-adjective and する-verb: 退屈な授業 (a boring class), 退屈する (to be bored). つまらない is more casual.
cards.example_sentence: 雨の日曜日は、退屈でしかたがない。
cards.example_reading: あめ の にちようび は、 たいくつ で しかたが ない。
cards.example_meaning: Rainy Sundays are unbearably boring.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book (expected later in Ch.2): 三葉 is fed up with everyone watching her family.
cards.context: うんざりする; 〜にうんざりだ. Stronger than 嫌: you've had more than enough.
cards.example_sentence: 毎日同じ話を聞かされて、うんざりした。
cards.example_reading: まいにち おなじ はなし を きかされて、 うんざり した。
cards.example_meaning: I was sick of hearing the same story every day.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book (expected later in Ch.2): 三葉's longing for Tokyo and city life.
cards.context: Verb 憧れる (〜に憧れる = to long for, look up to). 憧れの先輩 = the senior everyone admires. 憧 = heart radical 忄 + 童.
cards.example_sentence: 都会の暮らしは、ずっと私の憧れだった。
cards.example_reading: とかい の くらし は、 ずっと わたし の あこがれ だった。
cards.example_meaning: City life had always been my dream.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book (expected later in Ch.2): 三葉 thinks about what she'll do after high school.
cards.context: 〜を卒業する = to graduate from (with を). 卒業式 = graduation ceremony. Figurative: to grow out of something.
cards.example_sentence: 高校を卒業したら、東京の大学に行きたい。
cards.example_reading: こうこう を そつぎょう したら、 とうきょう の だいがく に いきたい。
cards.example_meaning: After I graduate from high school, I want to go to a university in Tokyo.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book (expected later in Ch.2): The comet is approaching Earth.
cards.context: 地 (ground) + 球 (ball). 地球温暖化 = global warming.
cards.example_sentence: 月は、地球のまわりを回っている。
cards.example_reading: つき は、 ちきゅう の まわり を まわって いる。
cards.example_meaning: The moon goes around the Earth.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book (expected later in Ch.2): TV coverage of the comet arriving from space.
cards.context: 宇宙人 = alien; 宇宙飛行士 (うちゅうひこうし) = astronaut.
cards.example_sentence: いつか宇宙から地球を見てみたい。
cards.example_reading: いつか うちゅう から ちきゅう を みて みたい。
cards.example_meaning: Someday I want to see the Earth from space.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book (expected later in Ch.2): The comet is what everyone is talking about.
cards.context: 話題になる = to become a hot topic; 話題を変える = to change the subject.
cards.example_sentence: その映画は、今クラスで話題になっている。
cards.example_reading: その えいが は、 いま クラス で わだい に なって いる。
cards.example_meaning: That film is what everyone in class is talking about right now.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book (expected later in Ch.2): TV shows live coverage of the comet.
cards.context: 生中継 (なまちゅうけい) = a live broadcast. 中継する = to broadcast live / relay.
cards.example_sentence: サッカーの試合をテレビの生中継で見た。
cards.example_reading: サッカー の しあい を テレビ の なまちゅうけい で みた。
cards.example_meaning: I watched the soccer match live on TV.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book (expected later in Ch.2): The braided cords are made from many coloured threads — and the town itself is called 糸守.
cards.context: 毛糸 (けいと) = wool yarn; 糸を通す = to thread a needle. 糸 is the first kanji of 糸守 ('thread-guard').
cards.example_sentence: 母は赤い糸でボタンをつけてくれた。
cards.example_reading: はは は あかい いと で ボタン を つけて くれた。
cards.example_meaning: My mother sewed on the button for me with red thread.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book (expected later in Ch.2): 組紐 is a braided 紐 — and 三葉 ties her hair with one.
cards.context: 紐を結ぶ = to tie a string; 靴紐 (くつひも) = shoelace.
cards.example_sentence: 靴紐がほどけているよ。
cards.example_reading: くつひも が ほどけて いる よ。
cards.example_meaning: Your shoelace is untied.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book (expected later in Ch.2): The braiding and the ritual are old shrine traditions kept up by grandmother.
cards.context: 伝 (pass on) + 統 (lineage). 伝統的な = traditional; 伝統を守る = to keep a tradition alive.
cards.example_sentence: この祭りは、三百年続く町の伝統だ。
cards.example_reading: この まつり は、 さんびゃくねん つづく まち の でんとう だ。
cards.example_meaning: This festival is a town tradition that goes back three hundred years.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book (expected later in Ch.2): Grandmother's story: old records burned in a great fire, so the meaning of the rituals was lost.
cards.context: 記録する / 記録に残す = to keep on record. Also a sports record: 世界記録, 記録を破る (break a record).
cards.example_sentence: 昔の記録によると、この町には城があったらしい。
cards.example_reading: むかし の きろく に よる と、 この まち に は しろ が あった らしい。
cards.example_meaning: According to old records, this town apparently had a castle.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book (expected later in Ch.2): The old records burned in the great fire.
cards.context: Intransitive (something burns); transitive 焼く = to burn, grill. 日に焼ける = to get a tan; パンが焼ける = bread is baked.
cards.example_sentence: 火事で、家が全部焼けてしまった。
cards.example_reading: かじ で、 いえ が ぜんぶ やけて しまった。
cards.example_meaning: The whole house burned down in the fire.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book (expected later in Ch.2): The shrine's autumn festival night.
cards.context: 夏祭り, 秋祭り; お祭り (friendly/polite). 祭る (まつる) = to enshrine, worship.
cards.example_sentence: 祭りの夜、町は人でいっぱいだった。
cards.example_reading: まつり の よる、 まち は ひと で いっぱい だった。
cards.example_meaning: On the night of the festival, the town was full of people.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book (expected later in Ch.2): The sisters dress in shrine-maiden costume for the ritual.
cards.context: 衣 (garment) + 装 (attire). 民族衣装 = national costume; 花嫁衣装 = wedding dress.
cards.example_sentence: 劇のために、手作りの衣装を用意した。
cards.example_reading: げき の ため に、 てづくり の いしょう を ようい した。
cards.example_meaning: I prepared a handmade costume for the play.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book (expected later in Ch.2): Fits the ritual dance, where shrine maidens shake bells.
cards.context: A small round bell: 鈴が鳴る = a bell rings. A big temple bell is 鐘 (かね).
cards.example_sentence: 猫の首輪に小さな鈴をつけた。
cards.example_reading: ねこ の くびわ に ちいさな すず を つけた。
cards.example_meaning: I put a little bell on the cat's collar.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book (expected later in Ch.2): Making 口噛み酒: the chewed rice is spat out into a vessel — in front of everyone.
cards.context: 吐く (to spit, vomit, breathe out) + 出す (out). Figurative: 気持ちを吐き出す = to get your feelings out.
cards.example_sentence: 熱すぎて、思わずスープを吐き出した。
cards.example_reading: あつすぎて、 おもわず スープ を はきだした。
cards.example_meaning: It was so hot I spat the soup out without thinking.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book (expected later in Ch.2): A narration favourite — reactions that happen before anyone thinks.
cards.context: 思わず笑う / 思わず声が出る. Close to つい, which is more 'out of habit'.
cards.example_sentence: あまりにおかしくて、思わず笑ってしまった。
cards.example_reading: あまり に おかしくて、 おもわず わらって しまった。
cards.example_meaning: It was so funny that I burst out laughing.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book (expected later in Ch.2): 三葉 sighs a lot about her town and her family.
cards.context: ため息をつく = to sigh (use つく, not する).
cards.example_sentence: テストの点を見て、深いため息をついた。
cards.example_reading: テスト の てん を みて、 ふかい ためいき を ついた。
cards.example_meaning: I looked at my test score and let out a deep sigh.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: Fits the morning when 四葉 calls her big 'sister' to get up and come down to breakfast.
cards.context: Transitive partner of 起きる: 起きる = I get up; 起こす = I wake someone else up (母に起こされた = I was woken by my mother). Also 'to cause': 事故を起こす = to cause an accident.
cards.example_sentence: 明日は早いから、六時に起こしてくれる？
cards.example_reading: あした は はやい から、 ろくじ に おこして くれる？
cards.example_meaning: I have an early start tomorrow. Can you wake me up at six?

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: The rushed school morning: at this rate 'Mitsuha' will be late.
cards.context: 遅刻する = to be late for something on a schedule (school, work). 〜に遅れる also works: 授業に遅れる. 寝坊 (oversleeping, Ch.1) is often the reason.
cards.example_sentence: バスが来なくて、学校に遅刻してしまった。
cards.example_reading: バス が こなくて、 がっこう に ちこく して しまった。
cards.example_meaning: The bus didn't come, so I was late for school.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: 瀧 has to find his way around a town and a school he has never seen.
cards.context: 道に迷う = to lose your way. It also means 'can't decide': どれにするか迷う = can't decide which one to choose. 迷子 (まいご) = a lost child.
cards.example_sentence: 初めての町で道に迷って、交番で聞いた。
cards.example_reading: はじめて の まち で みち に まよって、 こうばん で きいた。
cards.example_meaning: I got lost in a town I'd never been to, so I asked at the police box.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: At school, 瀧 doesn't know which desk is 三葉's.
cards.context: 席に着く (つく) = to take your seat; 席を立つ = to get up from your seat; 席をゆずる = to give up your seat. 座席 (ざせき) = a seat on a train or in a theatre.
cards.example_sentence: 電車でお年寄りに席をゆずった。
cards.example_reading: でんしゃ で おとしより に せき を ゆずった。
cards.example_meaning: I gave up my seat to an elderly person on the train.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: 'Mitsuha' talks and moves like a rough boy, and her classmates can't believe it.
cards.context: な-adjective and noun: 乱暴な言葉 = rough language; 乱暴に扱う = to handle roughly. For speech, 言葉遣いが乱暴 is a common combination. 乱暴する can mean actual violence, so it's a strong word.
cards.example_sentence: 本を乱暴に扱わないでください。
cards.example_reading: ほん を らんぼう に あつかわないで ください。
cards.example_meaning: Please don't handle the books roughly.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: The classroom buzzes because 'Mitsuha' is acting like a completely different girl.
cards.context: 騒ぐ = to be noisy or worked up (教室で騒ぐ), or to make a fuss about something. 騒がしい = noisy; 大騒ぎ (おおさわぎ) = an uproar.
cards.example_sentence: 図書館で騒いではいけません。
cards.example_reading: としょかん で さわいで は いけません。
cards.example_meaning: You mustn't make noise in the library.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: Friends on both sides wonder whether 'Taki' and 'Mitsuha' have become different people overnight.
cards.context: 性格がいい / 明るい / 暗い = a good / cheerful / gloomy personality. 性格が変わる = to change as a person. 人柄 (ひとがら) is a warmer, more formal word.
cards.example_sentence: 姉と私は顔はそっくりだが、性格は正反対だ。
cards.example_reading: あね と わたし は かお は そっくり だ が、 せいかく は せいはんたい だ。
cards.example_meaning: My sister and I look exactly alike, but our personalities are complete opposites.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: 三葉 wakes up in a Tokyo apartment where 瀧 lives with just his father.
