cards.context: 父親 / 母親 are neutral words for someone's father / mother, common in narration. Your own father is 父 (ちち) in polite speech; someone else's is お父さん. 父親似 = takes after one's father.
cards.example_sentence: 彼は父親に似て、背が高い。
cards.example_reading: かれ は ちちおや に にて、 せ が たかい。
cards.example_meaning: He's tall, like his father.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: Instead of an old house in the mountains, 三葉 wakes up in a city apartment.
cards.context: False friend: マンション is an ordinary apartment block (usually concrete, several floors), not a 'mansion'. アパート = a smaller, cheaper building, often two storeys. 十階 (じゅっかい) = the tenth floor.
cards.example_sentence: うちのマンションの十階からは、富士山が見える。
cards.example_reading: うち の マンション の じゅっかい から は、 ふじさん が みえる。
cards.example_meaning: You can see Mt Fuji from the tenth floor of our apartment building.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: From the window and the streets, 三葉 takes in the Tokyo view she has only ever seen on screens.
cards.context: Irregular reading: 景色 = けしき. 景色がいい = there's a great view. 風景 (ふうけい) is similar but more 'the scene as a picture'; 夜景 (やけい) = a night view of city lights.
cards.example_sentence: 山の上から見た景色は、本当にきれいだった。
cards.example_reading: やま の うえ から みた けしき は、 ほんとう に きれい だった。
cards.example_meaning: The view from the top of the mountain was really beautiful.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: Tokyo's morning trains and stations are packed, which is a shock for a girl from a small town.
cards.context: Usually in the ている form: 電車が混んでいる = the train is crowded. Also written 込む. Opposite: 空いている (すいている) = not crowded. 混雑 (こんざつ) is the formal noun.
cards.example_sentence: 朝の電車はいつも混んでいて、座れない。
cards.example_reading: あさ の でんしゃ は いつも こんで いて、 すわれない。
cards.example_meaning: The morning train is always crowded, so I can't get a seat.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: Fits 三葉's first Tokyo commute through a maze of train lines.
cards.context: 〜で…に乗り換える = to change to … at ~ (新宿で中央線に乗り換える). Noun: 乗り換え = a transfer. The hard Ch.4 word 乗り継ぐ means making connections on a long journey.
cards.example_sentence: 東京駅で新幹線に乗り換えてください。
cards.example_reading: とうきょうえき で しんかんせん に のりかえて ください。
cards.example_meaning: Please change to the bullet train at Tokyo Station.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: Huge Tokyo crossings full of people, a world away from Itomori's quiet roads.
cards.context: 交 (cross) + 差 + 点 (point). 交差点を右に曲がる = to turn right at the intersection. 信号 (しんごう) = traffic light; 横断歩道 (おうだんほどう) = pedestrian crossing.
cards.example_sentence: 次の交差点を左に曲がると、駅があります。
cards.example_reading: つぎ の こうさてん を ひだり に まがる と、 えき が あります。
cards.example_meaning: Turn left at the next intersection and you'll find the station.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: 司 and 高木 can tell their friend isn't his usual self today.
cards.context: 普段は = normally; 普段の〜 = everyday ~ (普段の生活, 普段着 ふだんぎ = everyday clothes). いつも = always; 普段 = as a rule, in daily life.
cards.example_sentence: 普段はおとなしい彼が、今日は大きな声で笑っていた。
cards.example_reading: ふだん は おとなしい かれ が、 きょう は おおきな こえ で わらって いた。
cards.example_meaning: He's normally quiet, but today he was laughing loudly.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: Every time 三葉 slips into girl-speech in front of 瀧's friends, she has to laugh it off.
cards.context: 笑ってごまかす = to laugh something off; 年をごまかす = to lie about your age; お金をごまかす = to cheat someone out of money. The kanji 誤魔化す is rarely used.
cards.example_sentence: 宿題を忘れたことを、笑ってごまかした。
cards.example_reading: しゅくだい を わすれた こと を、 わらって ごまかした。
cards.example_meaning: I laughed it off when I'd forgotten my homework.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: Embarrassing moments on both sides leave faces burning red.
cards.context: 顔が真っ赤になる = to go bright red. 真っ + a colour makes it stronger: 真っ白 (まっしろ), 真っ黒 (まっくろ), 真っ青 (まっさお, pale with fear). Note the special reading まっか.
cards.example_sentence: みんなの前で名前を呼ばれて、顔が真っ赤になった。
cards.example_reading: みんな の まえ で なまえ を よばれて、 かお が まっか に なった。
cards.example_meaning: When my name was called in front of everyone, my face went bright red.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: After school, 三葉 gets to visit a stylish Tokyo café, exactly what she dreamed of.
cards.context: な-adjective: おしゃれな店 = a stylish shop. Also a noun / する-verb: おしゃれする = to dress up. The kanji お洒落 is rare. The hard deck's 洗練 is the formal word for 'refined'.
cards.example_sentence: 駅の近くに、おしゃれなカフェができた。
cards.example_reading: えき の ちかく に、 おしゃれな カフェ が できた。
cards.example_meaning: A stylish café has opened near the station.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: Ordering at the café, and later taking orders as a waiter.
cards.context: 注文する = to order. ご注文は? = What would you like? (a waiter's phrase). In casual speech people often say 頼む: コーヒーを頼む.
cards.example_sentence: ご注文はお決まりですか。
cards.example_reading: ごちゅうもん は おきまり です か。
cards.example_meaning: Are you ready to order?

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: Tokyo café prices are a surprise for a girl used to small-town costs.
cards.context: 値段が高い / 安い (not 大きい / 小さい). 値段を聞く = to ask the price. 値段 is the everyday word; 価格 (かかく) is formal and used on price tags.
cards.example_sentence: このケーキはおいしいけど、値段がちょっと高い。
cards.example_reading: この ケーキ は おいしい けど、 ねだん が ちょっと たかい。
cards.example_meaning: This cake is delicious, but it's a bit expensive.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: 瀧 works part-time as a waiter at an Italian restaurant, and 三葉 has to cover his shift.
cards.context: Short for アルバイト (from the German Arbeit). バイトする = to work part-time; バイト先 = where you work part-time. パート is the usual word for adults' part-time work.
cards.example_sentence: 週に三回、駅前のパン屋でバイトしている。
cards.example_reading: しゅう に さんかい、 えきまえ の パンや で バイト して いる。
cards.example_meaning: I work part-time at the bakery in front of the station three times a week.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: 奥寺先輩 is the older, much-admired co-worker at 瀧's restaurant.
cards.context: Anyone who started school or work before you. It's also used as a title: 奥寺先輩. Opposite: 後輩 (こうはい) = junior. 同期 (どうき) = someone who started at the same time.
cards.example_sentence: バイト先の先輩に、仕事を丁寧に教えてもらった。
cards.example_reading: バイトさき の せんぱい に、 しごと を ていねい に おしえて もらった。
cards.example_meaning: A senior co-worker at my part-time job taught me the work carefully.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: 奥寺先輩 is the restaurant's beautiful, popular senior.
cards.context: Normally said of women. 美しい is the adjective 'beautiful'. イケメン (Ch.1) is the casual word for a handsome man.
cards.example_sentence: 彼女のお姉さんは、町で有名な美人だ。
cards.example_reading: かのじょ の おねえさん は、 まち で ゆうめいな びじん だ。
cards.example_meaning: Her older sister is a well-known beauty in town.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: Restaurant customers, including one who causes serious trouble.
cards.context: Polite forms: お客さん (everyday), お客様 (staff speaking to customers). 客席 = seats for customers or an audience; 乗客 (じょうきゃく) = a passenger.
cards.example_sentence: 週末の店は、お客さんでいっぱいだった。
cards.example_reading: しゅうまつ の みせ は、 おきゃくさん で いっぱい だった。
cards.example_meaning: The shop was full of customers on the weekend.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: Covering a waiter's shift she has never done before, 三葉 struggles to avoid mistakes.
cards.context: 失敗する = to fail, to mess up. ミスする is casual and used for small slips. Saying: 失敗は成功のもと = failure is the first step to success.
cards.example_sentence: 初めての仕事で、たくさん失敗した。
cards.example_reading: はじめて の しごと で、 たくさん しっぱい した。
cards.example_meaning: I made lots of mistakes at my first job.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: Saying sorry to customers is part of the job, even in someone else's body.
cards.context: 〜に謝る = to apologize to someone. 謝罪 (しゃざい) is the formal noun. The same kanji is in 感謝 (かんしゃ, gratitude). Staff apologize with 申し訳ございません (very polite).
cards.example_sentence: 約束を忘れて、友だちに謝った。
cards.example_reading: やくそく を わすれて、 ともだち に あやまった。
cards.example_meaning: I forgot our plans, so I apologized to my friend.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: A rude customer starts complaining and giving the staff a hard time.
cards.context: 文句を言う = to complain. 文句なし = perfect, no complaints. The hard deck's クレーム is a complaint made to a business; 文句 is everyday grumbling.
cards.example_sentence: 弟は、晩ご飯が遅いと文句を言っている。
cards.example_reading: おとうと は、 ばんごはん が おそい と もんく を いって いる。
cards.example_meaning: My little brother is complaining that dinner is late.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: The troublesome customer makes things hard for everyone in the restaurant.
cards.context: 迷惑をかける = to cause someone trouble; 迷惑な客 = a nuisance customer; ご迷惑をおかけしました = sorry for the trouble (a set apology). 迷 is the same kanji as in 迷う.
cards.example_sentence: 夜遅くに大きな音を出すと、近所に迷惑だよ。
cards.example_reading: よる おそく に おおきな おと を だす と、 きんじょ に めいわく だ よ。
cards.example_meaning: Making loud noises late at night bothers the neighbours.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: 奥寺先輩 is left with a torn skirt after the customer slashes it.
cards.context: Intransitive: something tears. Transitive 破る = to tear, and also to break a promise or rule (約束を破る). Use 破れる for cloth and paper; 切れる for things that snap or are cut.
cards.example_sentence: 転んだときに、ズボンのひざが破れた。
cards.example_reading: ころんだ とき に、 ズボン の ひざ が やぶれた。
cards.example_meaning: When I fell, the knee of my trousers ripped.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: With a needle and thread, 三葉 in 瀧's body repairs 奥寺先輩's skirt.
cards.context: 針に糸を通す = to thread a needle. 時計の針 = the hands of a clock; 釣り針 (つりばり) = a fishing hook; 注射針 = a syringe needle.
cards.example_sentence: 細い針に糸を通すのは、なかなか難しい。
cards.example_reading: ほそい はり に いと を とおす の は、 なかなか むずかしい。
cards.example_meaning: Threading a fine needle is pretty difficult.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: Instead of panicking, 'Taki' calmly fixes the ruined skirt.
cards.context: Intransitive pair: 直る = to get fixed. Also 'to correct': 間違いを直す. Vます + 直す = to redo: 書き直す, 言い直す. For curing an illness, use 治す (same reading).
cards.example_sentence: 父は、こわれた自転車を自分で直した。
cards.example_reading: ちち は、 こわれた じてんしゃ を じぶん で なおした。
cards.example_meaning: My father fixed the broken bicycle himself.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: Nobody expected 'Taki' to be so good with a needle. It's a surprising side of him.
cards.context: な-adjective: 意外な一面 = an unexpected side of someone. 意外と / 意外に = surprisingly: 意外と簡単 = surprisingly easy. The opposite idea is 予想通り = just as expected.
cards.example_sentence: 怖そうな先生だったが、話してみると意外に優しかった。
cards.example_reading: こわそうな せんせい だった が、 はなして みる と いがい に やさしかった。
cards.example_meaning: The teacher looked scary, but when I talked to him, he was surprisingly kind.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: Everyone is impressed by how neatly 'Taki' sews up the tear.
cards.context: 感心する = to admire someone's skill, effort or good behaviour (感動 = to be emotionally moved). Don't confuse it with 関心 (かんしん, interest): 政治に関心がある.
cards.example_sentence: 弟が毎朝早く起きて勉強しているので、感心した。
cards.example_reading: おとうと が まいあさ はやく おきて べんきょう して いる ので、 かんしん した。
cards.example_meaning: I was impressed that my little brother gets up early every morning to study.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: 奥寺先輩 praises 'Taki' for his surprising skill.
cards.context: 人を褒める; passive 褒められる = to be praised. Often written in kana: ほめる. Opposite: 叱る (しかる) = to scold.
cards.example_sentence: テストでいい点を取って、先生に褒められた。
cards.example_reading: テスト で いい てん を とって、 せんせい に ほめられた。
cards.example_meaning: I got a good score on the test, and the teacher praised me.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: 奥寺先輩 thanks 'Taki' for getting her out of a bad situation.
cards.context: お礼を言う = to say thank you; お礼をする = to give something back as thanks. The kanji 礼 is also in 失礼 (しつれい) and 礼儀 (れいぎ, manners).
cards.example_sentence: 手伝ってくれたお礼に、ケーキを買ってきた。
cards.example_reading: てつだって くれた おれい に、 ケーキ を かって きた。
cards.example_meaning: I bought a cake to thank you for your help.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: Back in their own bodies, both check their phones and find things they never wrote.
cards.context: Short for 携帯電話. スマホ (smartphone) is now just as common. 携帯する = to carry (formal); 携帯用 = portable, for carrying.
cards.example_sentence: 携帯を家に忘れて、一日中不便だった。
cards.example_reading: けいたい を いえ に わすれて、 いちにちじゅう ふべん だった。
cards.example_meaning: I left my phone at home and it was a pain all day.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: Notes and diary entries left behind by the other person are the first clues.
cards.context: Transitive; the intransitive pair is 残る = to remain. メモを残す = to leave a note; ご飯を残す = to leave food uneaten; 伝言を残す = to leave a message.
cards.example_sentence: 母は「先に寝ます」とメモを残して、寝てしまった。
cards.example_reading: はは は 「さき に ねます」 と メモ を のこして、 ねて しまった。
cards.example_meaning: My mother left a note saying 'Going to bed first' and went to sleep.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: Each of them is sure they never wrote those entries, yet there they are on the phone.
cards.context: 確かに = for sure; also used to agree: 確かにそうだね = you've got a point. Without に, 確か means 'if I remember right': 確か三時だった. 確かめる (to check) uses the same kanji.
cards.example_sentence: 確かに私の字だが、書いた覚えがない。
cards.example_reading: たしか に わたし の じ だ が、 かいた おぼえ が ない。
cards.example_meaning: It's definitely my handwriting, but I don't remember writing it.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: Someone has been doing whatever they like with your body, your friends and your day, without asking.
cards.context: 勝手に使わないで = don't use it without asking. 勝手な人 / 自分勝手 = a selfish person. It can also mean 'by itself': ドアが勝手に開いた = the door opened on its own.
cards.example_sentence: 人の日記を勝手に読まないで！
cards.example_reading: ひと の にっき を かって に よまないで！
cards.example_meaning: Don't read my diary without asking!

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: The scary thought that someone else, a total stranger, was living in your body.
cards.context: 他人 = anyone who isn't you, often with an 'outsider' feel: 赤の他人 = a complete stranger; 他人のふり = acting as if you don't know someone. Compare 別人 (Ch.3) = a different person from before.
cards.example_sentence: 他人の意見ばかり気にしていたら、何も決められない。
cards.example_reading: たにん の いけん ばかり き に して いたら、 なにも きめられない。
cards.example_meaning: If you only worry about other people's opinions, you can't decide anything.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: 'Could it be…?' The suspicion grows that the dream is no dream at all.
cards.context: Introduces a guess you half believe: もしかして〜? = could it be ~? or 'by any chance': もしかして田中さんですか. もしかしたら = maybe (just a possibility). For stronger disbelief, use まさか.
cards.example_sentence: もしかして、あの人は昨日駅で会った人じゃない？
cards.example_reading: もしかして、 あの ひと は きのう えき で あった ひと じゃない？
cards.example_meaning: Could that be the person we met at the station yesterday?

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: Swapping bodies with a stranger? At first, neither of them can believe it.
cards.context: 〜を信じる. 信じられない = I can't believe it / unbelievable. 信じ込む = to firmly believe (often wrongly). 信用 (しんよう) = trust.
cards.example_sentence: 宝くじが当たったなんて、まだ信じられない。
cards.example_reading: たからくじ が あたった なんて、 まだ しんじられない。
cards.example_meaning: I still can't believe I won the lottery.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: Once the clues pile up: so it really did happen after all.
cards.context: Casual form of やはり, which is more written or formal. Means 'just as I thought' or 'after all (I changed my mind)': やっぱりやめる = on second thought, I won't. Even more casual: やっぱ.
cards.example_sentence: 迷ったけど、やっぱり赤いほうを買うことにした。
cards.example_reading: まよった けど、 やっぱり あかい ほう を かう こと に した。
cards.example_meaning: I couldn't decide, but in the end I went with the red one.
